description: Filming started before the screenplay was actually finished. The crew leaned so hard on the story beats and action that most of the dialogue got worked out on the day, take after take, with Favreau happy to let it happen because it made everything feel less rehearsed.

title: Cue Cards in the Desert
description: That cocky monologue Tony gives the troops while showing off the Jericho missile wasn't scripted, it came together right there on set. And those sunglasses he's wearing aren't just for the desert sun, Downey was also using them to sneak glances at cue cards.

title: Coulson Was Meant to Be a Nobody
description: Phil Coulson was written as such a minor character that he wasn't even given a surname to start with, just 'Agent'. Clark Gregg clicked so well with the rest of the cast during filming that the part kept getting bigger, eventually growing into a whole spin-off show.

title: The Mandarin Was the Original Plan
description: Marvel was so confident the Mandarin would be the villain that Favreau announced it at San Diego Comic-Con back in 2006. Plans shifted, though, and by the time cameras rolled the antagonist duties had gone to Obadiah Stane instead, with the Mandarin held back for a later film.

title: A $200 Million Student Film
description: Jeff Bridges is a famously prepared actor, so having no real script to work from freaked him out at first. He eventually made peace with it by telling himself he was just part of a very expensive student film, and once he reframed it that way, he said it turned out great.

title: Paul Bettany Never Watched the Movie
description: The man behind JARVIS's voice has apparently never sat through Iron Man and doesn't really know what happens in it. He's described the job as the easiest paycheck of his career, just a couple of hours in the booth before heading off on holiday with his wife.

title: Rhodey's Ringtone Is a Deep Cut
description: Next time Tony calls Rhodey, listen closely. His ringtone is a MIDI rendition of the theme song from the 1966 Iron Man cartoon, a tiny nod buried in the sound design that most people scroll straight past.

title: 450 Pieces of Armor
description: The practical Mark III suit worn on set wasn't one solid shell, it was built from roughly 450 individual pieces fitted together, which is part of why suiting Downey up for shots took so long.

title: Real Childhood Photos in the Montage
description: The quick flashback montage of Tony Stark's life isn't just movie-magic photoshopping, editor Kyle Cooper wove in genuine childhood photographs of Robert Downey Jr. with his own father, Robert Downey Sr.

title: Faking the Arc Reactor Surgery
description: For the scene where Pepper swaps out Tony's arc reactor, the crew rigged up a prosthetic chest piece that connected to Downey's real torso and jutted out at an angle behind the chair he sat in, with a bright light aimed at the seam to hide the join.

title: Why JARVIS Isn't Human
description: In the comics, Jarvis is Howard Stark's loyal human butler. The film turned him into an AI partly as a nod to that legacy and partly to dodge the obvious comparison to Batman's butler Alfred, since a wisecracking computer voice reads pretty differently on screen.

title: Tony Stark Was Basically Howard Hughes
description: Stan Lee has said he built the original comic version of Tony Stark around Howard Hughes, someone he saw as one of the most colourful figures of his era: inventor, playboy, multimillionaire, and eventually a full-blown eccentric.

title: Five Suits, All Comic Accurate
description: The film runs through roughly five different armor variants, and every one of them is pulled from the comics in some way. The gold-only look JARVIS shows off first is a wink to the classic 'Golden Avenger' era, while the finished red and gold design echoes the 1980s Silver Centurion armor.

title: Roxxon Hiding in Plain Sight
description: During the highway brawl with Iron Monger, keep an eye on the buildings in the background, one of them is branded with the Roxxon logo. In the wider Marvel universe, Roxxon is a shady energy conglomerate that's been tied to all sorts of dodgy dealings.

title: Favreau's 70-Pound Celebration
description: Once Jon Favreau landed the director's chair, he marked the occasion by going on a serious health kick, dropping about 70 pounds before production got underway.

title: Thirty Writers Said No
description: Before the film found its footing, around thirty different writers took a pass at the project and walked away. A lot of them figured Iron Man was too obscure a character to build a movie around, and plenty were nervous about signing on with a studio that had only ever made comic books.

title: SHIELD Got a Modern Rewrite
description: Coulson rattles off SHIELD's full name as the 'Strategic Homeland Intervention, Enforcement and Logistics Division.' That's actually a tweak on the comics, where the acronym has shifted over the decades from its original Cold War-era meaning to something a bit more current.

title: Marvel Bet on Itself
description: This was the first movie Marvel Studios financed entirely on its own, rather than licensing a character out to another studio. It was also the opening chapter of a planned six-picture distribution deal with Paramount, which later got reshuffled once Disney bought Marvel outright.

title: Cap's Shield on the Workbench
description: In the scene where Pepper walks in on Tony stripping off the damaged armor, Captain America's shield is sitting right there on his workbench. It showed up in several early trailers too, but Marvel quietly cut it out of the marketing before release.

title: The Post-Credits Scene Was Meant to Be Missed
description: Kevin Feige deliberately tucked Nick Fury's Avengers Initiative cameo after the credits so it wouldn't overshadow the main film if the bigger universe plans never panned out. He was stunned by how fast it blew up anyway, with outlets covering it within days.

title: Nobody Expected It to Be a Hit
description: Early projections had the film capping out around $100 million domestically for its entire run. It ended up making nearly that much in just its opening weekend alone and kept going from there, a result that genuinely surprised the people who greenlit it.

title: A Premiere in Disguise
description: Marvel exec Isaac Perlmutter famously avoided cameras and interviews, but he wasn't about to miss opening night for the studio's first film. He reportedly showed up at the premiere wearing a fake mustache and glasses so he could watch it happen without being recognised.

title: Toy Companies Weren't Sold on Iron Man
description: Marvel's whole business plan hinged on merchandise, but toy manufacturers weren't convinced a guy in a metal suit would move units before the film actually came out. One exec later said they basically couldn't give the license away, right up until the movie proved them wrong.

title: A Cheeseburger Over a Hospital Bed
description: The first thing Tony asks for after being rescued from months of captivity in Afghanistan isn't medical attention, it's a cheeseburger. A small moment, but it says everything about who this character is before he's even suited up.

title: One Actor, No Auditions
description: Joss Whedon didn't shortlist anyone for Ultron. James Spader was his one and only pick from day one, apparently because Spader's got this weirdly hypnotic voice that can sound calm and menacing one second and dry and funny the next. Spader used his own natural speaking voice for the recording sessions rather than putting on anything artificial.

title: A Year-Long Chase for Quicksilver
description: Getting Aaron Taylor-Johnson to sign on as Pietro Maximoff wasn't quick at all, ironically. Whedon reportedly spent close to a year courting him for the part. Taylor-Johnson eventually said yes partly because his Godzilla co-star Elizabeth Olsen had already been cast as his on-screen twin, Wanda.

title: The Fox Legal Tangle Behind Quicksilver
description: Because Fox owned the X-Men film rights and Quicksilver is technically Magneto's son, Marvel had to walk a tightrope. The deal struck between the studios meant this version of Pietro could never be called a mutant, and no line could tie him back to the X-Men or his comic dad, even though Fox had their own speedster running around in Days of Future Past at basically the same time.

title: Three Black Widows on Set
description: Scarlett Johansson was pregnant while shooting this, so the crew front-loaded a lot of her scenes early in production before it started to show and brought in three separate stunt doubles for the physical stuff later on. The doubles apparently looked so much like her that even her co-stars got confused, with Chris Evans admitting he'd sometimes start chatting to one of them mid-scene before realising it wasn't Scarlett at all.

title: A Rig Just for Eye Contact
description: Ultron was meant to tower at eight or nine feet tall on screen, but James Spader is only five foot ten in real life. To help his co-stars actually know where to look while acting opposite him, he wore a tall wire contraption strapped to his back with two red balls on top, roughly marking where Ultron's eyes would eventually sit once the CGI was added.

title: Edgar Wright's Cut Credits Scene
description: Before he left the Ant-Man project, Edgar Wright actually wrote an after-credits scene intended for this film. It never made it into the finished cut, and details on what it would have shown have stayed pretty scarce ever since.

title: Ultron's Wakanda Plan That Got Scrapped
description: Early drafts of the script had Ultron travelling to Wakanda himself to steal the vibranium he needed. That idea got dropped in favour of introducing the arms dealer Ulysses Klaw as the middleman instead, which is why Klaw ended up being the one holding a stash of the metal for Ultron to take by force.

title: The Loki Cameo Nobody Saw
description: Tom Hiddleston actually shot a full day of footage reprising Loki for one of Thor's vision sequences. Test audiences ended up finding the scene confusing, with some walking away thinking Loki had somehow been behind Ultron's creation the whole time, so the whole thing got cut way down and Loki's part in it vanished entirely.

title: Executives vs. the Farmhouse
description: Marvel's higher-ups weren't fans of Hawkeye's farm reveal or the team's vision sequences and reportedly threatened to cut them entirely unless Whedon added in the subplot with Thor visiting the cave. Once test screenings reacted badly to that cave detour, the studio turned around and ordered it trimmed anyway, leaving the editor to stitch together a version that still made sense without it.

title: Seoul Rolled Out the Red Carpet
description: The Seoul city government offered the production some pretty generous tax incentives to film there, which is a big part of why the Korean set pieces made it into the finished movie at all.

title: Hulk Nearly Flew the Quinjet Into Space
description: An earlier version of the ending had the Hulk piloting the Quinjet off into space rather than just wandering off on his own. Marvel apparently nixed it because they didn't want fans reading it as a setup for a Planet Hulk adaptation, which is a bit funny given where his story eventually did go years later.

title: Jocasta's Cameo on a Loading Screen
description: Keep an eye on Tony's monitor when he's cycling through AI options before settling on FRIDAY. One of the cards flashing past is labelled JOCASTA, a nod to the comics where Jocasta is a robot built by Ultron who eventually joins the Avengers herself.

title: Stan Lee Says His Catchphrase for the First Time
description: During the party scene where the Avengers are mingling with war veterans, Stan Lee shows up in his usual cameo spot and, for the first time in any MCU movie, actually gets to say his famous "Excelsior!" line out loud.

title: Saoirse Ronan Was Almost the Scarlet Witch
description: Before Elizabeth Olsen was locked in, Saoirse Ronan was reportedly floated as a possibility for the role of Wanda Maximoff. It's an interesting road not taken given how different the tone of that casting might have felt.

title: Cap Nearly Moves the Hammer
description: During the party game where everyone takes turns trying to lift Mjolnir, Steve Rogers is the only one who manages to budge it slightly before letting go, a small but deliberate nod toward the comic storylines where Captain America has actually proven worthy enough to wield the hammer himself.

title: War Machine Flies Solo
description: This is the first MCU outing where James Rhodes suits up as War Machine without either Pepper Potts or Happy Hogan anywhere nearby, a small detail that quietly separates it from his earlier Iron Man appearances.

title: Ultron's Red Hood Callback
description: When Ultron is lounging on his makeshift throne talking down to Pietro and Wanda, he's draped in a red hooded cloak. It's a subtle wink toward his first-ever comic appearance back in Avengers #54 from 1968, where he disguised himself under the alias "the Crimson Cowl."

title: Ultron's Comic Creator Wasn't Tony Stark
description: In the source comics, Ultron is Hank Pym's creation, not Tony Stark and Bruce Banner's. The switch happened mostly for practical reasons: Michael Douglas was busy playing an older Hank Pym over in the upcoming Ant-Man film, so handing the creation credit to Stark and Banner made a lot more sense for how the shared timeline was shaping up.

title: Vision's Origin Gets Flipped
description: In the comics, Ultron builds Vision specifically to hunt down and destroy the Avengers. The movie flips that idea on its head, having Stark and Banner shape his intellect and Thor's lightning give him life, so instead of being a weapon against the team, Vision ends up helping them fight Ultron himself.

title: Grand Central Gets a New Statue
description: The famous Hermes statue at Grand Central Station was smashed to pieces during the Chitauri invasion in the first Avengers film. Look closely in this sequel and you'll notice it's been rebuilt, only now redesigned as a tribute to the first responders who helped out during that same Battle of New York.

title: Cap's Shield Has a Comic-Accurate Upgrade
description: The magnetic gauntlet that lets Cap yank his shield back to his arm feels like slick movie tech, but it's actually pulled straight from the comics, where Tony Stark built a similar magnet-based retrieval system for his star-spangled teammate long before this film came along.

title: Falcon's Missing Persons Joke
description: Sam Wilson pops up briefly here, joking that he's busy working "missing persons" cases while Cap handles the actual avenging. It's a low-key tease that he's quietly helping Steve track down Bucky Barnes, a thread that would pay off properly once Captain America: Civil War rolled around.

title: Hawkeye's Costume Is a Comic Mashup
description: Clint's new suit in this film borrows a bit from three different eras of the character: his classic comic-book costume, the Ultimates version fans first saw referenced in the original Avengers, and his stint running around as the masked vigilante Ronin.

title: Why There's No Real Post-Credits Scene
description: Both Kevin Feige and Joss Whedon went out of their way beforehand to tell audiences not to expect a post-credits scene this time. Whedon reasoned that the shawarma gag at the end of the first Avengers had already set an impossibly high bar, and he didn't want people sitting through ten extra minutes of credits only to walk away disappointed.

title: Black Widow Doesn't Even Try
description: During the hammer-lifting party game, every Avenger gives Mjolnir a go except Natasha, who sits it out entirely. It's a nice little inversion of an alternate-reality comic story where Black Widow is actually the one deemed worthy enough to pick it up.

title: The Second Most Expensive Movie Ever Made
description: Age of Ultron reportedly cost around $365 million to make, which at the time put it just behind Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides as one of the priciest films ever produced, even once you account for inflation.

title: The Mid-Credits Gauntlet Doesn't Quite Add Up
description: That brief mid-credits shot of Thanos grabbing the Infinity Gauntlet and grumbling "Fine, I'll do it myself" actually created a small continuity headache down the line. Infinity War later established the real Gauntlet wasn't forged until the dwarf Eitri built it on Nidavellir, and Thor: Ragnarok revealed the one sitting in Odin's vault was a fake all along, so co-director Joe Russo eventually explained this particular scene must be set on Nidavellir itself rather than Asgard.

title: A Right-Handed Glove Turns Left
description: Eagle-eyed fans noticed the Infinity Gauntlet glimpsed in Odin's trophy room back in the first Thor movie fits a right hand, while the one Thanos slips on during the credits here fits his left. It's a tiny detail that ended up fuelling years of fan theories about fake gauntlets and hidden vaults before later films sorted it all out.

title: Joe Russo's Own Daughter Plays Lila Barton
description: That little girl practicing archery with Clint in the cold open isn't just any child actor - it's Ava Russo, daughter of director Joe Russo. Nice bit of nepotism that actually pays off emotionally given what happens to the rest of the family seconds later.

title: The Opening Scene Was Cut From Infinity War First
description: That gut-punch opening with Hawkeye's family turning to dust was actually written for Infinity War. It got pulled because the editors felt that film was already jumping between too many characters, so it got saved and used to kick off Endgame instead.

title: RDJ Was The Only Actor Given The Full Script
description: Marvel is notoriously paranoid about leaks, and on Endgame they took it to another level - most of the cast only got the pages for their own scenes. Robert Downey Jr. was reportedly the sole actor trusted with the complete script front to back.

title: Writing Started During Civil War Shoots
description: Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely didn't just sit down one day and bang out Infinity War and Endgame. They started plotting both films years earlier during downtime on the Civil War set, scribbling ideas while the cast was off filming other scenes.

title: Sixty Pages Of Ideas Before A Word Of Script Existed
description: Before either film had a proper screenplay, the writing team had already compiled roughly 60 pages of concepts and possibilities for how the two-part finale could play out. A lot of that never made the cut, but it shows how much was thrown at the wall.

title: Tony's Snacking Was Basically All Improvised
description: Robert Downey Jr. has a habit of sneaking food onto set to keep himself going through long days, and a lot of Tony Stark's snack moments came from that habit rather than the script. The bit where he offers everyone food around the table apparently wasn't planned at all.

title: Paul Rudd Was Filming Two Marvel Movies At Once
description: Somehow Paul Rudd managed to juggle shooting Endgame and Ant-Man and the Wasp during overlapping windows. Keeping two separate Scott Lang timelines straight in his head while bouncing between sets sounds like a headache, but you'd never know it from the finished films.

title: "I Love You 3000" Came From RDJ's Real Kid
description: That line Morgan says to Tony wasn't dreamed up in a writers' room - Robert Downey Jr. mentioned that one of his own children says something similar to him at home, and the filmmakers loved it so much they wrote it straight into the movie.

title: A Grown-Up Morgan Scene Got Cut Entirely
description: At one point there was a scene inside the Soul Stone where a teenage Morgan Stark, played by 13 Reasons Why's Katherine Langford, tells her dad it's okay if he doesn't make it back. It's a mirror of the Thanos-and-young-Gamora scene from Infinity War, but it ended up on the cutting room floor rather than the final film.

title: Natalie Portman Never Actually Filmed For Endgame
description: That glimpse of Jane Foster you catch isn't new footage at all. It's an outtake recycled straight from Thor: The Dark World - Portman never stepped on set for Endgame, so her actual return had to wait for a later Thor film.

title: 1,400 VFX Artists Built The Final Battle In 16 Weeks
description: The massive portal battle where every hero shows up at once took roughly 1,400 visual effects artists working flat out, and they only had around sixteen weeks to pull it off. Given how much is happening on screen in that sequence, that's a genuinely wild turnaround time.

title: Endgame's First Character Borrowed From TV
description: James D'Arcy briefly pops up as Edwin Jarvis, and it's easy to miss why that's a big deal - he's actually reprising a role from the short-lived Agent Carter series. It was the first time a Marvel movie pulled a character over from one of their TV shows.

title: The Snap Was The Very Last Shot Filmed
description: Out of everything in this three-hour epic, the actual moment Tony snaps his fingers in the gauntlet was the last piece of footage captured for the whole movie, shot during reshoots in January 2019, with the visual effects team still finishing work on it right up until the premiere.

title: Robert Downey Jr. Refused To Give Tony A Death Speech
description: The writers apparently drafted a bunch of dialogue for Tony's goodbye scene, but Downey pushed back hard and insisted the moment land better with Tony saying nothing at all. It's part of why that scene hits as hard as it does - the silence does the work.

title: The Funeral Scene Wasn't Stitched Together In Post
description: With basically the entire MCU cast standing together at Tony's funeral, you'd assume some digital trickery was involved to get everyone in one shot. Nope - every actor was physically there on the same day, and the crew just shot five or six takes of the whole group.

title: Thor's Asgard Scene Was Shot Two Years Early
description: The corridor conversation between Thor and Rocket on Asgard was actually filmed at Durham Cathedral all the way back in April 2017, while the crew was still shooting Infinity War. It's one of the very few Endgame scenes that predates its own production.

title: Robert Redford Called It His Final Acting Role
description: When Robert Redford came back for his brief cameo, he apparently told the crew on set that this was going to be his last piece of on-camera acting before stepping away from the profession altogether.

title: The "Hail Hydra" Elevator Scene Is A Comics Callback
description: When Steve mutters "Hail Hydra" to get the scepter off Sitwell, it's not just a throwaway gag - it's a direct nod to the Secret Empire comic run, where the real Steve Rogers turns out to be a sleeper agent for Hydra and uses that exact phrase to prove his loyalty.

title: The Five-Year Jump Began As A "What If" Pitch
description: The whole idea of skipping five years ahead and showing everyone broken and scattered wasn't originally treated as the main plot. It started life as a side concept the writers jokingly called their "What If?" section back when they were first mapping out the two films.

title: There Was A Version Where Thanos Throws Cap's Severed Head
description: An early draft had a much darker beat where Thanos opens a portal to reveal he'd already been to the battlefield and tosses the head of the 2012 version of Captain America onto the ground in front of the heroes. Understandably, it never made it past the drawing board.

title: The Final Showdown Was Inspired By A Spaghetti Western
description: For the tense final standoff between Tony, Steve, Thor and Thanos, the Russo brothers said they were drawing on the classic tension-building style of Sergio Leone's Once Upon a Time in the West rather than anything from previous superhero movies.

title: The Curtain Call Credits Were A Star Trek Homage
description: That closing credits sequence where each actor's name appears over a still of their character wasn't a random stylistic choice - the filmmakers have said it was directly inspired by the way the original Star Trek TV series used to roll its cast credits.

title: Nineteen Oscar Winners Or Nominees Are In This Cast
description: For a superhero blockbuster, the acting pedigree on display is honestly kind of absurd - reports from the production put the number of Academy Award winning or nominated actors appearing in the film at nineteen.

title: Captain Marvel's Rescue Directly Continues Her Own Post-Credits Scene
description: The moment Carol Danvers shows up to save a drifting Tony Stark isn't a standalone beat - it picks up right where her post-credits scene left off, with her tracking down his ship using the beacon left over from Nick Fury's pager call.

title: Rockstar Confirmed Development Years Before Anyone Saw a Frame
description: Long before a single screenshot existed, Rockstar quietly told the world on the Newswire back on February 4th, 2022 that the next Grand Theft Auto was actively in the works. No name, no footage, just a short confirmation that set off years of speculation and countless fan theories about where it would be set.

title: Vice City's First Comeback Since 2006
description: Vice City hadn't been the main setting of a GTA game since Vice City Stories launched on the PSP way back in 2006. GTA VI marks its first return as a flagship, current-gen location, rebuilt from scratch and looking nothing like the pastel-soaked PS2 era version longtime fans remember.

title: The Trailer That Leaked Itself Out Early
description: Trailer 1 was originally scheduled for December 5th, 2023, but a shaky bootleg copy hit social media the night before. Rather than let the leak steal the moment, Rockstar scrambled and dropped the real, full-quality trailer just hours later on December 4th.

title: A YouTube Record That Beat MrBeast
description: Trailer 1 pulled in over 93 million views on YouTube within its first 24 hours, which was enough to set a Guinness World Record for the most-watched video game trailer ever and quietly overtake MrBeast's previous best of 59.4 million.

title: Trailer 2 Went Even Bigger Across Every Platform
description: When Trailer 2 dropped on May 6th, 2025, it racked up roughly 475 million views across all platforms combined in its first day. That figure counts everywhere the trailer was watched, not just YouTube, so it's not a direct apples-to-apples comparison with Trailer 1's numbers, but it's still a staggering reach for a single video.

title: The 2022 Slack Breach That Leaked 90 Videos
description: In September 2022 a hacker going by 'teapotuberhacker,' who also claimed responsibility for a recent Uber breach, broke into a Rockstar employee's Slack and dumped around 90 clips of early, unpolished GTA VI development footage onto GTAForums. It's still considered one of the biggest leaks in gaming history.

title: The Leak That Confirmed Lucia Before Rockstar Did
description: Long before Rockstar officially introduced her, that 2022 leak had already revealed the game would star a female protagonist alongside a male co-lead, giving fans their first unofficial glimpse of who we now know as Lucia and Jason.

title: A Second Leak Hit Just Months Before Launch
description: History repeated itself in August 2026 when another alleged hacker posted gameplay clips and what looked like a full map of Leonida online, warning other publishers that nobody was safe from the same kind of breach. Fans nicknamed the whole saga the 'Cyberleek' incident.

title: The Extended Look Premiered on Netflix, Not YouTube
description: Rockstar broke from tradition for its big pre-launch gameplay reveal, premiering 'Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look' on Netflix on August 27th, 2026, before letting it loose for free on YouTube and the official site a few hours later that same evening.

title: A Bonnie and Clyde Story With Jason and Lucia
description: Rockstar's own pitch for the story leans hard into Bonnie and Clyde territory: Jason and Lucia know the odds have always been against them, and when a simple job goes sideways they end up tangled in a criminal conspiracy across Leonida, with only each other to rely on to survive it.

title: Two Editions With a Real Price Tag Attached
description: Despite months of rumours that GTA VI could cost as much as $200, Rockstar settled on a Standard Edition priced at $79.99 and an Ultimate Edition at $99.99, putting it in line with other big current-gen console releases rather than the wild numbers fans had been bracing for.

title: Leonida Is Made Up of Six Named Regions
description: Rockstar has officially named six distinct areas that make up the state of Leonida: Vice City itself, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga National Park. An exact map size has never been published, so anything you see quoting square miles online is still just fan estimation.

title: It's Single-Player Only, At Least for Now
description: Rockstar has been very direct about this one: GTA VI launches as a single-player experience with no online mode included at release. A GTA Online-style follow-up is widely assumed to be coming eventually, but nothing has been named, dated, or confirmed for it yet.

title: No PC Version Has Been Announced Yet
description: As of launch, GTA VI is confirmed only for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar hasn't said a word about a PC release window, following the same pattern as GTA V, which didn't arrive on PC until well over a year after console.

title: A Wildlife Checklist Straight Out of Red Dead
description: Leonida's animal population is genuinely huge, with alligators, boars, dogs, snakes, flamingos, dolphins and even sharks confirmed. Spot or study them in the wild or at the zoo and they get logged to a checklist, a system that feels lifted almost straight out of Red Dead Redemption 2.

title: A Fully Explorable Zoo and Metro System
description: Among the confirmed landmarks players will be able to walk into are a full zoo, a working Vice City Metro Station, a massive airport, a football stadium, and a large military base, on top of the malls, hotels, nightclubs and pawn shops already shown off in trailers.

title: Switching Between Jason and Lucia Happens Mid-Action
description: When Jason and Lucia are together, control can jump between them almost instantly, even in the middle of a car chase, with one driving while the other leans out to shoot. Split them up, though, and switching goes back to that slower, GTA V-style transition sweeping across the map.

title: The Extended Look Was Shot Entirely on a PS5
description: That 26-minute Extended Look wasn't a cinematic trailer dressed up to look like gameplay, it was genuinely captured running on a PlayStation 5, giving fans the clearest indication yet of what the final game will actually look like in motion.

title: Over Ten Times More NPC Animation Than GTA V
description: Rockstar has reportedly built more than 600,000 individual NPC animations for GTA VI, compared to roughly 55,000 in GTA V. That jump is a big part of why pedestrians and crowds in the recent footage look so much less repetitive and robotic than in past games.

title: Backyard Wrestling Is an Actual Confirmed Activity
description: Alongside more expected pastimes like basketball, mini golf, scuba diving and kayaking, footage has confirmed a genuinely odd one: backyard wrestling complete with WWE-style finishing moves, plus base jumping and stock car racing for anyone who wants a bit more adrenaline.

title: Pre-Orders Came With a Vintage Vice City Bundle
description: Anyone who pre-ordered GTA VI, in either edition, got a bonus Vintage Vice City Pack thrown in along with a free month of GTA+. Only the boxed Standard Edition actually ships with a physical code inside, since every other version is entirely digital.

title: Guns and Masks Both Live on the Item Wheel
description: Small detail, but a telling one: masks have been pulled into the same item wheel used for weapons, and guns now automatically holster the moment you walk into a shop. It's a quiet convenience upgrade that suggests Rockstar spent real time smoothing out the friction points GTA V players complained about for years.

title: Built Under the Codename 'Big'
description: Once Naughty Dog wrapped up Jak 3, they pulled their most technically skilled staff together and quietly started working on something new under the internal codename 'Big'. Rather than just building another PS3 Jak and Daxter game, they wanted a fresh IP built around realistic human characters, which is how Drake and his adventures were born.

title: A Different Name in Japan
description: Over in Japan the game didn't even carry the Uncharted name. It was released as 'Uncharted: The Secret Treasure of El Dorado', dropping the Drake's Fortune subtitle entirely in favour of something a bit more literal.

title: The Strange Relic is a Jak and Daxter Callback
description: Tucked away near the start of the Fortress chapter is the Strange Relic, an egg-shaped treasure covered in odd symbols. Translate the markings and they actually spell out 'Naughty Dog' and 'Madman', and the whole thing is really a sly nod to the Precursor Orbs from the studio's earlier Jak and Daxter games.

title: Nate's Wetsuit Brand is an Ottsel in Disguise
description: Whenever Drake or Elena suit up in wetsuits, the brand stitched on is 'Ottsel'. That's not a made-up label either, it's a wink at Jak from Jak and Daxter, who happens to be part of the ottsel species.

title: NDI Stamped on Drake's Holster
description: Look closely at the back of Nathan Drake's holster and you'll spot the letters NDI branded onto it. It's a cheeky little in-joke standing for Naughty Dog Incorporated, hiding in plain sight on the character's own gear.

title: Sully's Seaplane Pays Tribute to Crash Bandicoot
description: Sully's trusty seaplane is named the Hog Wild, which isn't a random pick. It's lifted straight from a level of the same name in Crash Bandicoot, another Naughty Dog classic, giving longtime fans a little nostalgic nudge.

title: Sic Parvis Magna
description: Drake wears a ring around his neck engraved with Sic Parvis Magna, Latin for 'greatness from small beginnings'. It's introduced almost casually here, but the phrase becomes a genuine throughline for who Nathan Drake actually is by the time later games roll around.

title: A Throwaway Line That Was Actually Foreshadowing
description: Early on someone points out that Sir Francis Drake never actually had a family, and Nate just brushes it off. Play the later games and that offhand moment turns into proper foreshadowing, since it's eventually revealed Nate isn't a real descendant of Sir Francis at all, and 'Nathan Drake' isn't even his birth name.

title: The Real Sir Francis Drake's Coffin Is Still Missing
description: The historical Sir Francis Drake really was buried at sea in a lead coffin somewhere near Portobelo, Panama, and to this day nobody has ever found it. It's a nice bit of real-world mystery that lines up neatly with the treasure-hunting premise of the game.

title: The German Version Edited Out 'Nazi'
description: When the game got localized for Germany, the word 'Nazi' was scrubbed out of the dialogue entirely. It's a fairly common move for German releases dealing with that era, but it does mean a few lines land a bit differently for German players.

title: Drake Was Originally Modeled on Johnny Knoxville
description: Before Nathan Drake looked the way we know him, the design team was actually referencing Jackass star Johnny Knoxville. Lead designer Richard Lemarchand explained the team liked the mix of 'coolness and goodness' Knoxville gave off, and figured it fit exactly what they wanted Drake to be.

title: Nolan North Was Already a Naughty Dog Regular
description: Before he ever picked up Drake's holsters, Nolan North had already lent his voice to Naughty Dog, playing the mad scientist N. Gin across several Crash Bandicoot games. So when he walked in to audition for Uncharted, he wasn't exactly a stranger to the studio.

title: Amy Hennig and Richard Lemarchand Led the Charge
description: Amy Hennig directed the very first Uncharted, with Richard Lemarchand handling the design work alongside her. Between the two of them, they set the template for the pulpy, cinematic tone the whole series would end up chasing for years afterward.

title: A Spider Swarm Almost Made the Cut
description: For the Amazon ruins section, the team actually sketched concept art of Sully getting swarmed by spiders as a potential obstacle. It never made it into the finished game, but the idea didn't go to waste, since something very similar turned up years later in Uncharted 3.

title: The Final Boss Was Built to Fit the Island, Not the Other Way Around
description: In an old EGM interview, co-president Evan Wells admitted the ending boss fight was shaped by the confines of the island they'd already built, and that a bit more time might have let them do something flashier. Amy Hennig chimed in too, noting games often struggle with escalating to a climax the way movies don't have to.

title: Elena Almost Had Short Dark Hair
description: Elena Fisher wasn't always the blonde journalist players remember. Early in development she was designed as a short-haired brunette, and it was only fairly late in production that the team switched her over to the look that stuck for the rest of the series.

title: Nate Was Meant to Be Younger and Scrappier
description: The Nathan Drake originally on the drawing board was pictured as a guy in his twenties, which is part of why his voice was pitched a bit higher and his build a lot leaner than the Drake players actually got in the finished game.

title: Featured in '1001 Video Games You Must Play Before You Die'
description: Drake's Fortune earned itself a spot in Tony Mott's well-known book '1001 Video Games You Must Play Before You Die', sitting alongside a curated list of titles considered essential playing across gaming history.

title: A Million Copies in Ten Weeks
description: Drake's Fortune sold over a million copies within just ten weeks of hitting shelves, quickly earning it a place in the European Platinum Range of best-selling titles and proving Naughty Dog's gamble on a brand new IP had paid off.

title: The Script Was Written Around the Motion Capture Shoots
description: Nolan North has talked about how Amy Hennig was practically writing the story on the fly during motion capture sessions, shaping lines and scenes based on how the actors' performances were actually landing in the room rather than sticking rigidly to a finished script.

title: Six Award Nominations and Counting
description: Drake's Fortune picked up nominations across the board in its debut year, including a nod for Best PlayStation Game at the Spike Video Game Awards, a technical achievement nomination at the BAFTA Games Awards, and a Best Original Adventure Game win at the NAVGTR Awards.

title: The Sixaxis Controller Got Put to Work
description: Drake's Fortune leaned on the PS3's motion-sensing Sixaxis controller for some surprisingly hands-on moments, having players physically tilt the controller to lob grenades accurately or keep Drake balanced while creeping across narrow logs.

title: Drake's Fortune Shows Up Inside The Last of Us
description: Naughty Dog couldn't resist sneaking their own games into each other. In The Last of Us, players can find plush toys of Nathan Drake, Jak, and Daxter sitting alongside an actual Uncharted board game, tucked away on dorm room shelves for anyone bothering to search the rooms properly.

title: The Logo Hidden in the Blood
description: Early on when Drake and Tenzin stumble across a pile of dead wolves in the ice cave, don't rush past it. If you look closely at the blood splattered in the snow you'll spot a single red paw print sitting among the mess, which is actually a nod to the Naughty Dog logo itself, tucked into the scenery where most players never think to look.

title: Twelve Behind-the-Scenes Films
description: Sony didn't just ship the game and move on, they put out twelve short documentary segments covering how Naughty Dog actually built the thing, going into the motivation behind the story, the tech powering it and the acting process behind the mocap. The first batch shipped on the disc itself, with the rest trickling out online afterwards.

title: Revealed With a Marco Polo Twist
description: Game Informer broke the news on Uncharted 2 back in December 2008, and even then the outlet let slip that Marco Polo's real expeditions through Asia would be woven into the plot, long before anyone had actually played a second of it.

title: The First Teaser Was Just a Dagger in a Snowstorm
description: The very first teaser trailer, released December 1st 2008, showed almost nothing, just Drake reaching out for a dagger in the middle of a snowstorm, rendered in the actual in-game engine rather than a flashy pre-rendered cutscene.

title: The Second Teaser Spoiled the Whole Opening
description: Two weeks after the first teaser, a second one dropped showing a badly beaten up Drake waking inside a wrecked train car hanging over a cliff edge, basically giving away the game's now-iconic opening chapter months ahead of release.

title: Chloe and Her Voice Actress Share a Homeland
description: Chloe Frazer was written as having grown up in Australia, and it just so happens her voice and mocap actress Claudia Black is Australian too, hailing from Sydney, so there's a bit of genuine background matching the character.

title: A Very Different Title in Japan
description: Uncharted 2: Among Thieves didn't keep its name when it crossed the Pacific. In Japan it was localised as Uncharted: The Golden Sword and the Disappeared Fleet, which honestly sounds like a whole different pulp adventure novel.

title: Tenzin Breaks Robin Atkin Downes' Streak
description: Robin Atkin Downes has played villain after villain across the Uncharted series, so Tenzin sticks out. He's the loyal Tibetan guide who becomes one of Nate's genuine allies, making it the one time Downes gets to play someone actually on Drake's side.

title: Uncharted 2 Almost Had a Completely Different Name
description: Before Naughty Dog settled on Among Thieves, the sequel was floating around internally under the working subtitle Something Mysterious and Cool, which is a very Naughty Dog placeholder if ever there was one.

title: Multiplayer Skins Borrow From Other Sony Exclusives
description: The multiplayer DLC didn't just add more Drake and Chloe outfits, it let you run around as characters pulled from inFamous, Killzone and Resistance, plus a nod to a fictional Uncharted title called Eye of Indra that never actually existed as a real game.

title: Tenzin Is Named After a Real Everest Legend
description: Tenzin's name is a direct tip of the hat to Tenzing Norgay, the real Tibetan Sherpa who climbed Everest alongside Edmund Hillary and became one of the first two people ever confirmed to reach the summit.

title: The Borneo Mountains Are Based on a Real Peak
description: The mountainous Borneo section of the game takes its visual cues from the real Mount Kinabalu, even though in reality that peak sits way further north than where the game actually places Nate and Sully on the map.

title: The Istanbul Museum Is a Real Ottoman Palace
description: The museum Drake and Flynn sneak into during the Istanbul chapters is modelled on the Topkapi Palace Museum, once the actual seat of the Ottoman sultans and still one of the most visited landmarks in Turkey today.

title: "In Like Flynn" Is an Old Hollywood Joke
description: During the museum infiltration, Nate cracks a joke that they'll be "in like Flynn." It sounds like a throwaway pun on Harry Flynn's name, but it's actually a much older phrase tied to actor Errol Flynn and his reputation with the ladies.

title: 22 Months From Start to Finish
description: The whole game came together in just 22 months, with a solid 6 of those spent purely in pre-production before the team even got properly stuck into building levels.

title: The Tibetan Village Was Inspired by an Indie Art Game
description: Game designer Richard Lemarchand has said the quiet, reflective Tibetan village section drew inspiration from The Graveyard, a small 2008 art game about slowly walking an elderly woman through a graveyard, of all things.

title: Harry Flynn Roasts Drake's Weight
description: When Harry Flynn saves Nate from a botched jump in the second chapter, he cracks "you put on weight, mate" and tells him to lay off the doughnuts, a cheeky little reference to the Doughnut Drake multiplayer skin most players wouldn't even connect unless they'd already unlocked it.

title: Over 200 Game of the Year Wins
description: By the time the dust settled, Among Thieves had racked up more than 200 Game of the Year awards from outlets all over the industry, a haul that still gets brought up whenever people argue about the best games of that generation.

title: A Record-Setting Night at the Spike Video Game Awards
description: At the 2009 Spike Video Game Awards, Uncharted 2 pulled in a then-record eight nominations and walked away with three wins voted for entirely by fans, including the big one, Game of the Year.

title: Five Trophies at the Game Developers Choice Awards
description: At the 2010 Game Developers Conference, Uncharted 2 didn't just take the overall Game of the Year prize, it swept up five trophies total that night, also picking up wins for writing, audio, technology and visual art.

title: You Can Actually Play Marco Polo
description: Run past a rooftop pool during one of the city chapters and jump in, and Drake will actually start playing a round of Marco Polo, a playful little callback to the explorer's role in the first game. Naughty Dog liked the joke enough to bring it back years later in Uncharted 4.

title: A Chalkboard Quotes Homer's Odyssey
description: When Flynn tracks Nate down in the second chapter, keep an eye on the bar's chalkboard behind them, it reads "polytlas dios Nathan," a play on the ancient Greek epithet for Odysseus that roughly translates to Nathan the great sufferer, which, given everything Nate goes through in this game, feels pretty accurate.

title: Elena's Actress Wasn't Even Trying to Audition
description: Emily Rose landed the role of Elena Fisher almost by accident, she'd just tagged along to support a friend who was auditioning, and ended up getting cast herself thanks to the chemistry she showed reading opposite Nolan North.

title: The Cast Rehearsed Together Like a Film Shoot
description: Unlike the first game, which was shot in a fairly rough open shed setup, Among Thieves had the whole cast rehearsing and performing scenes together on a proper soundstage with three or four mocap cameras running, letting the actors improvise off each other the way they would on an actual movie set.

title: Naughty Dog Split Into Two Teams for the First Time
description: While the bulk of Naughty Dog was heads-down on Drake's Deception, a second smaller team inside the studio was quietly working on something completely different in the background. That project turned out to be The Last of Us. It's the first time in the company's history they'd split like this, and it's kind of wild to think both games were cooking at the same building at once.

title: The Desert Setting Was Chosen to Push the Tech
description: Creative director Amy Hennig has said the team deliberately went for a desert this time because sand, fire and water are some of the hardest 'organic' elements to fake convincingly with animation. Basically they picked the setting that would force them to get better at the stuff nobody else was doing well yet.

title: T.E. Lawrence Inspired the Whole Plot
description: Drake's Deception opens with a quote lifted straight from Seven Pillars of Wisdom, the real memoir of T.E. Lawrence (yep, the actual Lawrence of Arabia). His life story, chasing lost cities across the Arabian desert, basically became the blueprint for Nate's own obsession in this game.

title: First Uncharted With Stereoscopic 3D
description: If you had a 3D telly back in 2011, Drake's Deception had you covered. It's the first game in the series to fully support high-resolution stereoscopic 3D, letting the sandstorms and collapsing buildings pop out at you a bit more dramatically than usual.

title: One of the First Games to Use an Online Pass
description: Buy it used back in the day and you'd need to cough up for a PlayStation Network Pass just to get into multiplayer. Uncharted 3 was one of the earliest big titles to lean on this system, which Sony (and pretty much every publisher) quietly dropped a few years later once everyone realised how unpopular it was.

title: Sold Over Nine Million Copies
description: Commercially this one was a monster. Drake's Deception shifted more than nine million copies worldwide, putting it up there among the best-selling games the PS3 ever had.

title: Swept Up Game of the Year Awards Everywhere
description: Critics were basically falling over themselves for this game at the end of 2011. It picked up Game of the Year honours from a huge stack of outlets and award shows, on top of being one of the most decorated titles of that generation.

title: Marlowe's Secret Society Goes Back 400 Years
description: Katherine Marlowe isn't just some random villain with a grudge, she's the head of a shadowy British order that supposedly traces its roots back to Queen Elizabeth I's own inner circle, including her spymaster Francis Walsingham and the occultist John Dee. That's the whole reason her group has been hunting Iram of the Pillars for centuries before Nate ever showed up.

title: The Ring and the Cipher Disk Only Work Together
description: Nate's family ring isn't just sentimental jewellery, it's actually a key. The whole opening con is built around the fact that an old cipher disk only reveals its hidden message once Sir Francis Drake's ring is slotted into it, which is exactly why both Nate and Marlowe are so desperate to get their hands on it.

title: Young Nate's First Meeting With Sully
description: The flashback chapters show a teenage Nate, played by Billy Unger, trying to lift the Drake ring from a Cartagena museum and getting way out of his depth. That's the moment Sully steps in, and it's basically the origin story for the whole Drake and Sullivan partnership fans already knew from the earlier games.

title: Cutter Got Written Out Because of The Hobbit
description: Charlie Cutter was originally supposed to stick around for the whole story, but his voice actor Graham McTavish landed a role in Peter Jackson's Hobbit trilogy partway through production. Naughty Dog had to rewrite the back half of the game to write him out, which is why he vanishes from the plot the way he does.

title: Cutter's Of Mice and Men Line
description: Right at the start of Chapter 9, after Nate and Cutter have their scuffle, Cutter mutters something that sounds oddly literary: 'Next you'll be standing behind me with a gun, telling me about the rabbits.' It's a direct nod to Of Mice and Men, dropped in so casually most players run straight past it without clocking the reference.

title: The Overseer Newspaper in the Opening Pub
description: Slow down in the London pub at the very start of the game and have a look at the background props. There's a newspaper called The Overseer lying around with a headline about scientists struggling to understand a deadly fungus, a tiny throwaway prop most people never bother to actually read.

title: Houdini Software Built the Flood Effects
description: Naughty Dog's engine could only handle 580 joints per mesh, which was a problem when they needed a big, realistic-looking flood surface for one of the game's set pieces. The VFX team turned to Houdini to fracture the water simulation into smaller pieces that could actually run in-game, then stitched it all back together so it still looked like one continuous surface.

title: Dry Docks Was Originally a Cut Singleplayer Level
description: The multiplayer map Dry Docks actually started life as a rough blockmesh layout designer Junki Saita was testing out for a singleplayer level. When that level idea got dropped, the layout was too good to waste, so it got reworked into a competitive multiplayer map instead.

title: The 'Well, Well, Well' Running Gag
description: Whenever the crew stumbles across an actual well in Drake's Deception, Sully can't resist cracking the same dad joke, 'well, well, well.' It became such a fan favourite bit that the 2022 movie brought it back almost word for word, just handing the line to Nate instead of Sully this time round.

title: Nolan North Wrote a Behind-the-Scenes Book
description: To tie in with the launch, Nathan Drake's own voice actor Nolan North put together a 128-page coffee table book called Drake's Journal, packed with over 500 photos from the motion capture stage. It even had QR codes printed inside that linked out to dozens of uncut mocap videos, which was a pretty novel idea for 2011.

title: Mocap and Dialogue Were Recorded Together, Like a Film Shoot
description: Naughty Dog ran production more like a movie set than a typical game shoot. They had a dedicated stage at Sony Pictures Studios where actors performed motion capture and recorded dialogue at the exact same time, cast together in the room doing full rehearsals before locking in final takes.

title: Fans Auditioned to Design a Multiplayer Character
description: Sony ran an actual competition where fans from the US and Europe pitched their own character for the multiplayer roster. Sixteen finalists made it through to a live audition at Sony's studios, judged by a panel that included Amy Hennig, Justin Richmond, Emily Rose and Nolan North himself.

title: The Cargo Plane Scene Got Recreated in the Movie
description: The sequence where Nate is clinging on for dear life inside a crashing cargo plane over the desert is one of the most talked-about set pieces in the whole series, and it's basically lifted shot-for-shot into the 2022 Tom Holland movie's opening. The film swaps the ending slightly (parachute versus plunging into the ocean), but it's unmistakably the same scene.

title: Multiplayer Servers Went Dark in 2019
description: Naughty Dog announced in June 2019 that Drake's Deception's online servers would be switched off that September, closing the book on nearly eight years of competitive and co-op multiplayer.

title: Nolan North Cameos in the 2022 Movie
description: Right after the movie recreates that cargo plane sequence, Nate and Chloe wash up on a beach and bump into a random sunbather who nods along like he's heard it all before. That's Nolan North himself, the actual voice of Drake in the games, getting a blink-and-you'll-miss-it cameo in a scene lifted from his own game.

title: The Stage Fright Trophy
description: There's a trophy called Stage Fright that pops up in Chapter 11 if you just stand still for 30 seconds after a certain cutscene. It's Naughty Dog poking fun at themselves, referencing the famously awkward E3 2015 stage demo where the controller froze up mid-presentation.

title: Nadine's Race Was Decided After Casting
description: Laura Bailey landed the role of Nadine Ross before the character's final look was locked in. A concept artist later sketched her as a Black woman, and Neil Druckmann liked the direction, but the team worried about backlash over a white actress voicing a Black character. It wasn't until they saw Bailey's actual performance that they decided it worked and kept her in the role.

title: A New Composer Took Over the Score
description: This was the first mainline Uncharted where Greg Edmonson didn't handle the main score. Henry Jackman stepped in instead and wrote a new take on Nate's Theme, blending the old melody with a rougher, more piratey feel for a track simply titled A Thief's End.

title: Even the Menu Music Changed
description: Small detail, but a telling one: this is the only mainline Uncharted game where the classic Nate's Theme doesn't play over the main menu at all, a quiet signal of just how much changed behind the scenes for this entry.

title: Three Relics, Three Naughty Dog Franchises
description: Hidden throughout the campaign are three collectible 'Strange Relics,' and each one is a sly nod to a different chapter of Naughty Dog's history. Find all of them and you get a trophy just for appreciating the studio's back catalogue.

title: A Precursor Orb Shows Up in Chapter 12
description: Keep an eye out during Chapter 12 and you'll spot a Precursor Orb, the glowing collectible that drives the plot of the old Jak and Daxter games. It's just sitting there for anyone who bothers to look.

title: A Wumpa Fruit Hidden in Chapter 21
description: Crash Bandicoot's favourite snack makes an appearance too. Search around in Chapter 21 and you'll find a Wumpa Fruit tucked away as a collectible, a cheeky throwback to the game that put Naughty Dog on the map in the first place.

title: A Firefly Dog Tag Turns Up on a Skeleton
description: One of the game's more macabre little jokes is a skeleton carrying a Firefly dog tag, the same faction symbol from The Last of Us. Nobody ever explains how it ended up in a remote corner of the Uncharted world, and that's kind of the fun of it.

title: Nate Plays the Original Crash Bandicoot
description: Early in Chapter 4, you can find Nate and Elena's home console set up with a fully playable, emulated version of the original PS1 Crash Bandicoot. You can actually take control of Crash yourself, and it's mapped to the D-pad rather than a thumbstick, matching how the game was originally controlled back in 1996.

title: Marco Polo Makes a Comeback
description: If you steer your boat toward the larger of the two islands in Chapter 12, you can trigger a game of Marco Polo between Nate and Elena, a playful callback to a similar moment fans loved back in Uncharted 2.

title: A Comic Poster That Sparked Ellie Pregnancy Theories
description: In Nate and Elena's daughter's bedroom hangs a poster for a fictional comic called The Last of Us: American Daughters, showing a red-haired, visibly pregnant woman holding a revolver. Fans latched onto the resemblance to Ellie and spent years speculating it was foreshadowing for The Last of Us Part II, though that turned out not to be the case.

title: A Nod to Ellie's Favourite Comic
description: Same bedroom, another hidden reference: a poster reading 'Starlight Savage 2: Coming Soon.' Starlight Savage is the fictional comic series Ellie is obsessed with in The Last of Us, quietly tying the two worlds together on a kid's bedroom wall.

title: Pill Bottles That Point to The Last of Us Part II
description: This one went unnoticed for years. A Reddit user eventually spotted that some pill bottles you can examine in Uncharted 4 are labelled as coming from Weston's Pharmacy, a location that shows up again in The Last of Us Part II, released five years later.

title: Two Directors Left Mid-Development
description: The Uncharted 4 that shipped isn't the one that started production. Longtime series writer Amy Hennig and Uncharted 3 director Justin Richmond both departed partway through, and Neil Druckmann and Bruce Straley, fresh off The Last of Us, were brought in to take over and reshape the project.

title: The Original Version Had No Gun at the Start
description: Under Amy Hennig, the early version of the game leaned much harder into stealth and traversal, with Nate not even carrying a gun at the start, just his grappling hook and climbing gear. It was reportedly a deliberate attempt to dial back the gun violence that earlier Uncharted games had been criticised for.

title: Two Actors Were Cut After the Director Change
description: Graham McTavish, reprising his role as Charlie Cutter, and Alan Tudyk had already filmed scenes for the earlier version of the game before Amy Hennig's departure. Once their contracts were voided along with the change in direction, neither character made it into the final release.

title: Sam Drake Wasn't Always Troy Baker
description: Before Troy Baker took over the role, Todd Stashwick was cast as Sam Drake and even appears as the character's voice in the very first teaser trailer. When the game changed direction, Stashwick was quietly replaced.

title: One Actress, Two Roles
description: Merle Dandridge pulls double duty in this one, voicing and performing both Evelyn and Sister Catherine, two characters who never share the screen at the same time.

title: The Villain Is Based on a Real Pirate
description: Henry Avery isn't a Naughty Dog invention. He's built on the real historical figure Henry Every, a 17th-century English pirate whose exploits were so notorious that he became one of the most wanted men on the planet.

title: The Real Heist Behind the Story
description: The historical Henry Every is credited with pulling off what's considered the most profitable pirate raid ever recorded, ambushing a Mughal treasure convoy in the Arabian Sea in 1695 and walking away with a fortune worth tens of millions in today's money.

title: Libertalia Wasn't Entirely Made Up Either
description: The pirate utopia at the heart of the game's plot is drawn from old, mostly unverified legends about a real pirate colony called Libertalia, said to have been founded in Madagascar and run on ideals of liberty shared among its outlaw residents.

title: Faces Got a Massive Tech Upgrade
description: Naughty Dog rebuilt its facial animation system from scratch for this game. Where faces in The Last of Us and Uncharted 3 relied on roughly 90 to 100 animation points, Uncharted 4's characters use somewhere between 300 and 500, letting the team capture far subtler expressions.

title: A First for Naughty Dog's Cinematics
description: This was actually the first Naughty Dog project built with a dedicated facial capture setup, separate from full-body motion capture, a shift that helped push the studio's cinematics closer to photorealism than anything they'd made before.

title: A Trophy That Jokes About Its Own Violence
description: Fans had spent years poking fun at how a lighthearted adventure hero racks up such a huge body count, so Naughty Dog leaned into the joke with a trophy literally called Ludonarrative Dissonance, awarded for killing 1,000 enemies across the game.

title: A Bible Verse Runs Through the Whole Story
description: A line from Luke 23:41 gets referenced repeatedly throughout the game as a kind of thematic anchor, tying into the story's ideas about guilt, self-justification, and whether any of the treasure-hunting characters actually deserve redemption.

title: One Playthrough, Over 500 Kills
description: One journalist tallied up their own playthrough and came away having killed 527 enemies, more than three times the commonly cited body count for Indiana Jones across his entire film series, a fun bit of perspective on just how violent these adventure games really are.

title: The Fastest-Selling PS4 Exclusive of Its Time
description: In its first week alone, the game sold through more than 2.7 million copies worldwide across disc and digital, making it the fastest-selling first-party PS4 title released up to that point.

title: Nearly 9 Million Copies by Year's End
description: By December 2016, just seven months after launch, Sony reported the game had sold through more than 8.7 million copies worldwide, folding in physical, digital, and console bundle sales.

title: Born as DLC
description: This one almost never existed as its own game. Naughty Dog originally pitched it as a piece of paid DLC for Uncharted 4, something in the vein of a smaller side story, before the team realised they had way more to say than a DLC pack could hold and turned it into a full standalone release instead.

title: No Nathan Drake Required
description: For the first time in the series, you're not playing as Nathan Drake at all. Chloe Frazer, who'd only ever been a supporting character back in Uncharted 2 and 3, finally gets to run the show, with Nate nowhere to be found.

title: Chloe's Complicated Dad
description: Chloe's trust issues have deep roots. In the game's own backstory, her father was an archaeologist who became fixated on a treasure hidden in India, abandoned his family and sent Chloe and her mum off to Australia, then died still chasing the very thing he gave everything up for.

title: Calling Nadine 'China'
description: Keep an ear out and you'll notice Chloe refers to Nadine as 'china' a few times through the game. It's not a random nickname, it's old South African slang for mate or buddy, tracing back to Cockney rhyming slang ('china plate' = 'mate') that made its way into South African English, which lines up neatly with Nadine's background.

title: Breaking the Explorer Quote Tradition
description: Every mainline Uncharted game opens with a quote from a real historical explorer. This is the first one in the series to skip that tradition entirely, since the story doesn't really tie back to any single famous adventurer the way the others did.

title: Five Teams, One Location
description: Some of Uncharted 4's biggest open areas had to be scaled back because of time pressure. For The Lost Legacy, Naughty Dog restructured how it built environments, letting as many as five separate teams work on a single location at once so the game's big open space wouldn't suffer the same fate.

title: The Biggest Sandbox Naughty Dog Had Built
description: The Western Ghats hub area that Chloe and Nadine drive through wasn't just a bigger version of Uncharted 4's jeep sections, at the time of release, Naughty Dog described it as the largest open space the studio had ever put together for a game.

title: Eleven Tokens to Find
description: Tucked around the open-world Western Ghats section are eleven Hoysala Tokens, and hunting down every last one rewards players who fully explore the map rather than just racing to the next story beat.

title: The Protagonists That Almost Were
description: Before settling on Chloe, Naughty Dog kicked around a few other ideas for who should lead this spin-off, including Victor 'Sully' Sullivan, Uncharted 3's Charlie Cutter, and even Cassie Drake, Nathan and Elena's daughter, who'd only been glimpsed as an adult in Uncharted 4's epilogue.

title: Cassie Was Nearly the Star
description: There was genuine internal discussion about making Cassie Drake the lead instead of Chloe. The idea got dropped for a few reasons: the team worried she'd feel too much like a Lara Croft clone, an adult Cassie suddenly gunning down mercenaries felt tonally wrong, and honestly, Nate and Elena would never sign off on their daughter living that life.

title: The Skull From Left Behind
entertainment: The Last of Us: Left Behind
description: Partway through Chapter 8, after a nerve-wracking grapple swing off a crumbling tower, drop down into a small hidden nook below the branch instead of continuing on. There's a collectible plastic skull waiting there that you can shake like a Magic 8-Ball for a little fortune. It's the same Strange Skull toy that first popped up in The Last of Us: Left Behind.

title: Naughty Dog's Fifth Time Around
description: This was actually a first for the studio in a different way too, it's the first time Naughty Dog ever pushed one of its own franchises to a fifth mainline entry, since their earlier series either stopped after one game or got handed off to other developers.

title: Chloe's Heritage Confirmed
description: The game finally fills in a piece of Chloe's background that had only ever been hinted at before, confirming she's half-Indian and half-Australian, which gives her hunt for the Tusk of Ganesh a much more personal weight than just another treasure job.

title: Henry Jackman Returns to Score It
description: Composer Henry Jackman, who'd scored Uncharted 4 the year before, came back for The Lost Legacy and wove regional Indian musical textures into his usual sweeping adventure sound to match Chloe and Nadine's trip through the Western Ghats.

title: Nineteen Tracks of Swashbuckling
description: The official soundtrack runs to nineteen tracks, running just over an hour, with titles like 'Chloe Frazer', 'The Western Ghats' and 'The Tusk of Ganesh' mapping neatly onto the game's key characters and locations.

title: Marco Polo Makes a Comeback
description: The old Marco Polo minigame, first seen as a lighthearted moment between Nate and Elena back in Uncharted 2, shows up again here as a small optional distraction, a nice quiet callback for anyone who's been with the series a while.

title: Asav's Voice Actor Plays a Lot of Villains
description: Usman Ally, the Obie Award-winning stage actor behind antagonist Asav, has built a career out of playing bad guys across TV and film, and that experience shows in just how calm and unsettling he manages to make the character sound.

title: Meenu's Voice Actor's Big Break
description: Meenu, the sharp young girl Chloe crosses paths with while shopping in India, was a brand new character created for this game, and voicing her marked actress Tierra Rorls's very first video game role.

title: A Shelf Full of Award Nods
description: The game picked up recognition well beyond gaming's usual circles, landing nominations at the BAFTA Games Awards for Best Performer for both Claudia Black and Laura Bailey, plus nods from the Annie Awards, the Visual Effects Society and The Game Awards.

title: From PS4 to PC, Five Years Later
description: It launched on PS4 in August 2017, but the game's journey didn't stop there, a remastered PS5 version arrived in January 2022 as part of the Legacy of Thieves Collection, followed by a PC release that October, letting a whole new wave of players hunt for the Tusk of Ganesh.

title: Same Moves, Different Person
description: Naughty Dog made a deliberate choice to keep Chloe's core gameplay near-identical to Nate's, same weapons, same melee, same traversal, but they still put real care into her climbing, fighting and general movement so she'd feel like her own person rather than a reskin.

title: Sniff Out Treasure With a Gadget
description: There's an unlockable item in this one that pulses whenever a nearby treasure is worth investigating, a handy little nudge for anyone who wants to comb through every corner of the Western Ghats without missing loot.

title: What's Inside the Lockboxes
description: Scattered supply crates and lockboxes across the game usually hold ammo and grenades, but crack one open with the simple lock-picking minigame and you might land some of the best guns around, including the Silenced Pistol, an RPG, the China Lake shotgun-launcher, or the Harbinger sniper rifle.

title: Tryndamere Is Named After a Riot Co-Founder
description: The Barbarian King shares his name with Marc "Tryndamere" Merrill, one of Riot Games' co-founders. It's not the only bit of himself he worked into the lore either, since he also picked the name for Tryndamere's in-game wife.

title: Ashe Is Named After Marc Merrill's Real Wife
description: League's iconic Frost Archer owes her name to Ashley, the real-life wife of Riot co-founder Marc Merrill. He's even referenced it himself online, joking about being married to the actual Ashe. Naturally, the lore team went ahead and married her to Tryndamere in-game too.

title: Ezreal Is Named After a Real Riot Employee's Nickname
description: The Prodigal Explorer wasn't just plucked out of thin air. He's named after Colt Hallam, a Riot Games staffer who's gone by the nickname Ezreal for years, and who worked on some of the earliest systems in the game, including the original ARAM mode.

title: Lee Sin Draws From an Old Blind Monk Legend
description: Lee Sin's whole design leans on an older folk tale about a blind but incredibly skilled monk who fights through senses other than sight. It fits him perfectly, a martial artist who's lost his eyes but never lost his edge, relying on instinct and discipline instead.

title: Nasus and Renekton Are Modelled on Egyptian Gods
description: The jackal-headed Nasus is a clear nod to Anubis, the Egyptian god tied to death and the afterlife, while his crocodile brother Renekton borrows from Sobek, who ancient Egyptians prayed to for safe passage across the Nile. Two brothers, two very different gods, and a rivalry that's baked right into the mythology they're drawn from.

title: Annie Was Inspired By an Anime Sorceress
description: Before Annie became the tiny fire-wielding girl with a bear, she took cues from Lina Inverse, the explosive teenage sorceress from the anime Slayers. Riot originally planned for Annie to be a teenager too, but they eventually settled on a younger child instead, and looking at her now it's hard to imagine her any other way.

title: One of Veigar's Skins Is a Sneaky Gandalf Reference
description: Veigar already plays like a pint-sized Black Mage, but his eagle-rider skin takes things further with a not-so-subtle wink at Gandalf, specifically the moment he gets airlifted by a giant eagle in The Lord of the Rings. Swap the wizard's robes for a yordle and you've basically got the same picture.

title: Corki's Design Started as a Warcraft III Unit
description: Corki's little propeller helicopter isn't an original idea, it's lifted almost directly from the Dwarven Gyrocopter unit in Warcraft III, a game a lot of early Riot staff had cut their teeth on before making League. The bushy moustache and bomb-dropping playstyle carried over pretty much intact.

title: Riven's Story Mirrors Aragorn's Journey
description: Strip away the Noxian armour and Riven's arc looks a lot like Aragorn's. Both were exiled from where they belonged, both carried a broken blade as a symbol of who they used to be, and both eventually get that sword reforged as part of reclaiming their identity.

title: Akshan's Name Comes From Ancient Sanskrit
description: Akshan's name translates roughly to "eye" in Sanskrit, a nod to Hindu mythology where Shiva's mostly-closed third eye is said to unleash devastating power whenever it opens. Riot's champion team has talked about wanting more South Asian representation in the roster, and Akshan's very name is where that story starts.

title: There's a SOLD Sign on a Discontinued Item in the Shop
description: Take a proper look at the shop on the Red side base and you'll spot the old Heart of Gold item sitting there with a SOLD sign slapped over it. The item itself got removed from the game years ago, but Riot never bothered clearing the shelf, so it's just been sitting there ever since, technically bought by nobody and collected by no one.

title: There's a Hidden Statue Holding an Old Item on Blue Side
description: Head out of Blue side's base through the middle tower and take a right, and there's a big statue wearing a necklace with a stone set into it. That stone used to represent the Philosopher's Stone item, which later got renamed to Nomad's Medallion, but the statue itself was never updated, so it's quietly kept the old design in place.

title: An Item Was Once Named After a Famous WoW Streamer
description: Athene's Unholy Grail wasn't always called that. It started out as the Chalice of Discord before Riot renamed it in honour of Athene, a well-known World of Warcraft streamer who reportedly brought thousands of players over into League. Not a bad way to say thanks.

title: Rammus Used to Have a Full Set of Voice Lines
description: The armadillo everyone knows for saying "ok" over and over didn't start out that way. Rammus originally had a much bigger voice set with proper lines, but at some point Riot scrapped most of it, leaving him with the stripped-down, deadpan personality players have come to love.

title: Amumu Almost Wasn't a Yordle
description: Early drafts of Amumu's backstory described him as a mummified human child rather than a Yordle, which is a considerably darker starting point than what shipped. Riot eventually softened the concept, but even as a Yordle he's still stuck wandering the world alone, cursed and crying, so it's not exactly a cheerful ending either way.

title: Zyra Has Hidden Interactions Tied to Plants vs. Zombies
description: Zyra's kit is quietly full of little Easter eggs most players never notice. Killing, or being killed by, Karthus or Sion nets an extra bit of gold as a wink to Plants vs. Zombies, and if Maokai's on her team she gives him a small movement speed boost, since apparently plants look out for each other.

title: Malphite's Ground Slam Leaves the Riot Games Logo Behind
description: Next time you're playing against a Malphite, watch the ground when he slams down his ultimate. The crack pattern it leaves behind is shaped like Riot Games' own logo, a small piece of studio branding hidden in plain sight that most people run straight past without ever clocking it.

title: Four Champion Skins Are Named After Old Web Browsers
description: Foxfire Ahri, Chrome Rammus, Explorer Ezreal, and Safari Caitlyn line up a little too neatly with Firefox, Chrome, Internet Explorer, and Safari. Whether it's a deliberate in-joke from the skins team or just a happy coincidence, poor Ezreal really did get stuck representing the one browser everybody loves to complain about.

title: Rumble Named His Mech After His Crush on Tristana
description: According to Rumble's lore, he's had a soft spot for Tristana for a while now, enough that he named his rocket-powered mech Tristy after her. Naming a giant piece of battle machinery after your crush is a bold move, though whether it's actually worked in his favour is left pretty ambiguous.

title: Morgana and Kayle Are Actually Sisters
description: The Fallen and the Righteous aren't just thematic opposites, they're siblings. Morgana refused to join Kayle's crusade against evil, and that single disagreement fractured their relationship for good, eventually turning them into two of the most opposed forces in Runeterra's story.

title: Bard Doesn't Actually Speak in Words
description: Every one of Bard's voice lines is really just chiming noises to anyone in Runeterra, since he's technically speaking in a voice mortal ears can't process. Only a handful of beings, mostly other celestials, can actually understand what the Wandering Caretaker is saying, which makes him a genuinely strange and lonely kind of hero.

title: Where the Name Actually Comes From
description: Diablo's name isn't some deep lore reference, it's just geography. Creator David Brevik grew up near Mount Diablo in California, and Blizzard North's studios in Redwood City and San Mateo weren't far from it either, so the name just kind of stuck.

title: The Cow Level Started as a Total Lie
description: Back when the original Diablo came out, players spread a rumour about a secret cow level hidden somewhere in the game. It was completely made up, but the joke got so big that Blizzard actually built a real one into Diablo II a few years later.

title: Whimsyshire, the Cow Level's Weird Cousin
description: Craft the Staff of Herding and use it on the pink lights between old and new Tristram, and you'll open a portal to Whimsyshire, a candy-coloured field full of teddy bears, unicorns and giant butterflies that turn out to be just as deadly as anything else in the game. It's basically Blizzard's way of keeping the old cow level joke alive.

title: The 'Cute' Level Has a Dark Secret in Its Music
