description: By the end of 2014, One Piece had officially become the best-selling manga series of all time in print, according to Guinness World Records, with close to 321 million copies sold. It didn't stop there either — within a few more years the franchise blew past its own record, crossing the 500 million mark worldwide.

title: Luffy's Voice Actor Is a Woman Who Also Voices Krillin
description: The rubbery, loudmouthed captain of the Straw Hats has been voiced since day one by Mayumi Tanaka, a woman. If her voice work sounds strangely familiar to Dragon Ball fans too, that's because she's also the voice behind Krillin, giving her a rare foot in two of anime's biggest long-running franchises at once.

title: There's a Real One Piece Gym in Tokyo
description: Tucked away in Shibuya is BragMen, a gym built to look like it's straight out of the Grand Line, complete with rope, crates, heavy chains and compass patterns worked into the floor. Even the dumbbells get in on the theme, shaped like the giant meat legs Luffy is constantly dreaming about eating.

title: You Can Book a One Piece Themed Wedding in Japan
description: In 2021, a Japanese wedding planning company called ESCRIT launched a package built entirely around the series. Guests get greeted with a wanted-poster style welcome sign, a life-size cutout of the crew, and a menu inspired by Sanji's cooking, so devoted fans really can tie the knot pirate-style.

title: Real Cities Hide Inside the World of One Piece
description: A lot of the islands the Straw Hats visit aren't purely fantasy. The Rommel Kingdom echoes London's cityscape, the Kuja's mountaintop castle draws from China's Hanging Temple, and Water Seven's canals and architecture are basically a love letter to Venice, right down to the boats replacing cars.

title: Olympic Athletes Have Cosplayed One Piece Moves
description: During the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, the fandom showed up in an unexpected place. Greek long jumper Miltiadis Tentoglou greeted crowds by striking Luffy's Gear Second pose, while American shot putter Payton Otterdahl channelled Franky, shouting 'Super!' before launching into his throw.

title: Gear 5 Was Inspired by Tom and Jerry
description: Oda has said the slapstick, cartoon-logic battle between Luffy and Kaido drew directly from watching Tom and Jerry. He initially worried that kind of pure physical comedy wouldn't fit a story where Kaido is meant to be deadly serious, but he found a way to let Luffy's newfound goofiness collide with Kaido's menace without undercutting either.

title: One Piece and Dragon Ball Once Shared a Comic
description: Oda's friendship with Dragon Ball creator Akira Toriyama went beyond mutual respect. In 2006 the two collaborated on Cross Epoch, a one-off short story that threw characters from both series into the same world, a genuine crossover between two of Shonen Jump's biggest names rather than just a fan mash-up.

title: Luffy, Goku and Toriko Shared a TV Special
description: The crossover love between these Jump heavyweights didn't stop at print. In 2013, Fuji TV aired 'Dream 9 Toriko & One Piece & Dragon Ball Z Super Collaboration Special,' putting Luffy, Goku and Toriko together on screen in a way that felt like a genuine event for fans who'd grown up with all three.

title: Armani Designed Costumes for a One Piece Film
description: For One Piece Film: Z in 2012, the fashion label A/X Armani Exchange teamed up with Oda to design outfits for the Straw Hat crew. It's an unusual pairing on paper, high fashion meeting a pirate cartoon, but it shows just how far the franchise's reach extended even over a decade ago.

title: Oda Met His Wife Because She Was Cosplaying Nami
description: At Shonen Jump Fiesta 2002, Oda crossed paths with Chiaki Inaba, who happened to be dressed as Nami for the event. The two hit it off and eventually married, which means one of the series' most iconic characters is tied, in a roundabout way, to how its creator met his own wife.

title: The First English Dub Wasn't From 4Kids
description: Most Western fans associate One Piece's early English localisation with 4Kids, but they weren't first. Singapore-based Odex actually secured the earliest official English dub of the anime back in 2003, a year before 4Kids' more widely remembered (and more heavily edited) version hit the air.

title: One Piece Has Bounced Around Its Own TV Schedule
description: One Piece has aired on Fuji Television in Japan since it premiered, but it hasn't sat still on the schedule. Over the decades the show's timeslot has been shifted four separate times, a small but telling sign of how a network keeps adjusting around a series that simply refuses to end.

title: Filler Episodes Have Dropped Off Massively
description: Before the story's big timeskip, Toei padded the anime with 58 filler episodes to keep pace with the manga. After the timeskip, that number dropped to just 18, and none of the newer filler arcs run longer than four episodes, a clear sign the studio leaned much harder into staying close to Oda's source material as the story matured.

title: One Piece Ditched Its Year-Round Schedule in 2026
description: For over two decades, new One Piece episodes aired continuously, week after week, all year long. That changed heading into the Elbaph Arc, when producer Ryuta Koike announced the show would move to two shorter broadcast blocks a year, capping new episodes at around 26 annually so the anime could better match the manga's own pacing instead of racing to fill a weekly slot.

title: The Studio Behind One Piece Also Shaped Miyazaki
description: Toei Animation, the studio bringing One Piece to screens since 1999, has been around since 1956. Long before the Straw Hats ever set sail, legends like Hayao Miyazaki and Isao Takahata cut their teeth working there, which makes One Piece just one entry, albeit a huge one, in a studio history stretching back to the earliest days of Japanese TV animation.

title: Oda Had Veto Power Over the Netflix Live-Action Show
description: Live-action anime adaptations have a rough track record, and fans were braced for the worst when Netflix announced its One Piece series. What changed the conversation was Oda's involvement as executive producer with actual veto power, letting him block anything that strayed too far from the spirit of the source material, which is a big part of why the show landed as well as it did with longtime fans.

title: Oda Plants Story Seeds Hundreds of Chapters Early
description: Long before Brook ever joined the crew, the Straw Hats crossed paths with a giant whale named Laboon in one of the earliest arcs of the series. It takes hundreds of chapters, and just as many anime episodes, before the connection between that whale and Brook's own backstory pays off, a level of long-game plotting that's become one of the show's defining traits.

title: Birmingham Almost Never Sees Birmingham
description: Despite being set entirely in Birmingham, most of the show was actually shot up in Liverpool and Manchester. The production team scouted the real city and decided modern Birmingham just doesn't look like 1920s Birmingham anymore, so they went hunting for grittier, more industrial backdrops in the North West instead.

title: Cillian Murphy's 3,000-a-Season Habit
description: Tommy Shelby is rarely seen without a cigarette hanging out of his mouth, and it turns out that adds up. Cillian Murphy had the props team count how many herbal, rose-scented smokes he got through in a single season, and the tally landed around 3,000. He doesn't actually smoke in real life; they're just mint and lemongrass rolled up to look the part.

title: Tommy's Haircut Went Viral, and Cillian Hates It
description: The short-back-and-sides look that basically launched a thousand barbershop requests wasn't something Cillian Murphy ever warmed to. He's said he finds the whole Tommy Shelby cut a bit horrifying, even as fans keep turning up to meet him sporting the exact same style.

title: The Real Gang Couldn't Afford Their Own Signature Weapon
description: The razor-blades-in-the-cap-peak trick that gives the show its name is probably a myth. Razor blades were a genuine luxury item for working-class Birmingham lads in that era, and the idea seems to trace back to a novel called A Walk Down Summer Lane rather than anything the actual gang did.

title: The Real Peaky Blinders Had Already Faded by the 1920s
description: In the show, the Shelbys run Birmingham unchallenged through the 1920s. In reality, the actual Peaky Blinders gang peaked back in the 1890s, and by the time the series is set, a much bigger outfit called the Birmingham Gang had taken over the streets instead.

title: Alfie and May Are Married in Real Life
description: Tom Hardy's Alfie Solomons and Charlotte Riley's May Carleton never actually share a romance on screen, but off screen the two actors are husband and wife. They met filming a BBC adaptation of Wuthering Heights back in 2009 and married in 2014, years before both turned up in Small Heath.

title: John and Michael Are Cousins on Screen, Brothers Off It
description: Joe Cole and Finn Cole play cousins John Shelby and Michael Gray, but they're actually real-life brothers cast into the same sprawling family. It's the kind of casting quirk that only really clicks once someone points it out.

title: Sam Neill Got Coaching from Two Famous Irishmen
description: Sam Neill was born in Northern Ireland but grew up in New Zealand, so nailing a convincing 1920s Irish accent for Inspector Campbell didn't come naturally. He leaned on fellow actors James Nesbitt and Liam Neeson to help him get it right, only for the accent to later be dialled back so the show would land better with American audiences.

title: Polly's Voice Is Basically Ozzy Osbourne
description: Helen McCrory needed a rock-solid Birmingham accent to carry Aunt Polly, so she went straight to the source and studied hours of interview footage of Ozzy Osbourne to get the cadence right. Considering how iconic her performance became, it clearly worked.

title: The Weinstein Logo Got Cut After the Scandal Broke
description: The Weinstein Company had handled the show's American distribution for years, but once the allegations against Harvey Weinstein went public, the production pulled the company's logo from the credits almost immediately, one of the earliest concrete industry reactions once the #MeToo story broke.

title: David Bowie Sent Cillian Murphy a Photo of Himself in a Peaky Cap
description: Bowie was apparently a genuine fan of the show and once sent Cillian Murphy a picture of himself wearing a cap with razor blades sewn into the peak. He also agreed to let a track from what turned out to be his final album feature in the series, but sadly passed away before he ever got to see it air.

title: The Theme Song Has Been Everywhere Except the 1920s
description: Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds' Red Right Hand is so tied to Peaky Blinders now that it's easy to forget it's been knocking around since 1994 and has turned up in a pile of other things, including The X-Files, Scream, Hellboy, and even the comedy Dumb and Dumber.

title: Jason Statham Nearly Joined the Shelby Family
description: Steven Knight wrote Peaky Blinders not long after directing Jason Statham in the film Redemption, and reportedly wanted him for the show. Statham's schedule wouldn't allow it, which might have been for the best given how central a convincing Brummie accent is to the whole thing.

title: Two Nolan Villains Ended Up in the Same Gang Show
description: Cillian Murphy played Scarecrow and Tom Hardy played Bane in Christopher Nolan's Batman trilogy, and both ended up leading rival factions in Peaky Blinders. Murphy even popped up briefly in The Dark Knight Rises alongside Hardy, so the overlap runs deeper than just the casting choice.

title: All That Fire Is a Deliberate Nod to Hell
description: The recurring flames that seem to follow Tommy Shelby around aren't just moody set dressing. Season two director Colm McCarthy has confirmed it's meant to draw a straight line between Tommy's criminal path and where it's ultimately taking him, spiritually speaking.

title: The Show Started With a Story From Steven Knight's Dad
description: Creator Steven Knight has said the whole idea grew out of something his father told him as a kid, about being handed a note as a nine-year-old and sent to deliver it to his uncles, the Sheldons, who eventually became the Shelbys of the show.

title: Peaky Blinders Was Built to Be the Opposite of Downton Abbey
description: Producer Laurie Borg has been pretty blunt about the show's positioning, saying the goal was to be the total opposite of Downton Abbey, which he's called about as dull as television gets. Where Downton kept things clean and genteel, Peaky Blinders leaned hard into grit and violence instead.

title: Steven Knight Won't Watch Other Crime Dramas
description: To keep his own vision for the show intact, creator Steven Knight has said he deliberately avoids watching other prestige crime dramas like The Wire or Boardwalk Empire, worried that their storytelling choices might bleed into his own writing without him noticing.

title: Snoop Dogg Once Talked Steven Knight's Ear Off About the Show
description: Among the show's more unexpected famous fans is Snoop Dogg, who reportedly invited Steven Knight over for a three-hour conversation about how Peaky Blinders' portrayal of gang life reminded him of what first drew him to gang culture growing up in Long Beach.

title: The Finale Is Planned to End With an Air Raid Siren
description: Steven Knight has described Peaky Blinders as the story of a family caught between two wars, and he's said the whole saga is meant to close on Birmingham's first air raid siren of the Second World War, putting the intended end date at around June 1940.

title: Adrien Brody Arrived With a Grudge in Season 4
description: Season four brought in Adrien Brody as Luca Changretta, an Italian-American mobster gunning for revenge against the Shelby family, one of the show's more Hollywood-heavy casting additions.

title: Winston Churchill Shows Up in the Show
description: A handful of characters woven into the series are based on real historical figures, and Winston Churchill is one of them, appearing across several episodes as Tommy's dealings pull him into the orbit of actual establishment power.

title: The Eden Club's Ceiling Took 30 Gallons of Gold Paint
description: For the glitzy Eden Club set, the production team painted a huge, low white ceiling in a real Liverpool venue with a specially mixed shade that took roughly 30 gallons to finish. The colour became known on set simply as "Peaky gold."

title: Tommy's Office Has a Hidden Godfather Tribute
description: The production designer built Tommy's office in season two around The Godfather's influence on purpose, right down to dressing a few oranges into the set. In Coppola's film oranges quietly signal that doom is coming, and the Peaky Blinders team snuck the same trick in as a little wink for anyone paying close attention.

title: London Scenes Were Never Filmed in London
description: Despite Tommy's storylines regularly taking him down to the capital, the production never actually shot any of the London scenes there. Every bit of "London" you see on screen was built or found somewhere else entirely.

title: Wednesday Choreographed Her Own Dance
description: That whole viral dance to 'Goo Goo Muck' wasn't handed to Jenna Ortega by a choreographer, she made it up herself. She pulled moves from Bob Fosse, Siouxsie Sioux and the goth kids she used to watch at 80s clubs, then stitched it all together into something that somehow feels exactly like Wednesday Addams.

title: A Nod to the Original Wednesday's Signature Move
description: Buried inside Jenna Ortega's dance routine is a quick tribute to Lisa Loring, the actress who played Wednesday back in the 1964 series. If you know Loring's little arm flick from the original show, you'll spot it snuck into the choreography.

title: That Dance Was Filmed Right After COVID
description: Jenna Ortega has said she'd only just come down with COVID before she had to shoot the now-iconic dance sequence, so every one of those sharp, controlled movements was performed while she was still feeling pretty rough.

title: Tim Burton Almost Directed the 1991 Movie
description: Before he ever touched Nevermore Academy, Tim Burton was actually approached to direct the 1991 Addams Family film. He turned it down because he was busy finishing Batman Returns, so the gig went to Barry Sonnenfeld instead, and Burton's Addams moment had to wait another three decades.

title: Jenna Ortega's Audition Was Covered in Fake Blood
description: Jenna Ortega jumped onto her Zoom meeting with Tim Burton straight after wrapping a gory scene on another project, so she was still splattered head to toe in fake blood. Burton, being Burton, thought it was hilarious rather than off-putting, and has said since that he can't picture anyone else playing the role.

title: The Double Finger Snap
description: To open the hidden passage into the Nightshades' meeting room, Wednesday snaps her fingers twice in rhythm. That's a direct lift from Vic Mizzy's theme tune for the original 1964 series, where the finger snaps were basically the show's whole percussion section.

title: Where the Name Wednesday Actually Comes From
description: Wednesday's name is pulled from the old 'Monday's Child' nursery rhyme, the one that says 'Wednesday's child is full of woe.' Given how the character carries herself, it's hard to think of a more fitting line to have named her after.

title: Christina Ricci Used to Be Wednesday Herself
description: Casting Christina Ricci as Miss Thornhill is a lovely bit of stunt casting when you remember she actually played Wednesday Addams in the 90s films. Watching the old Wednesday teach the new one is one of those details that only lands if you grew up on the movies.

title: Cousin Itt's Portrait Hides a Secret
description: Down in the Nightshades' basement hangout there's a portrait of Cousin Ignatius Itt, and it's not just decoration, there's a safe hidden behind it holding a document that ends up being a key clue in the mystery.

title: Wednesday's Pet Scorpion Nero
description: In the original 1964 series Wednesday kept a pet spider called Homer. The Netflix version swaps that for a story about a childhood pet scorpion named Nero, who Wednesday says was killed by bullies when she was six, a much darker spin on the same idea.

title: Pugsley Tied Up With an Apple, Again
description: Right in episode one, Wednesday finds Pugsley stuffed in a locker, tied up with an apple jammed in his mouth. That exact image shows up in the 1991 Addams Family movie too, just with the roles reversed since this time it's Wednesday who did the tying.

title: Archery Was Always the Addams Way
description: When Wednesday signs up for archery as her Nevermore extracurricular, it's a callback to Addams Family Values, where Wednesday and Pugsley treat bow and arrow practice as a pretty normal sibling bonding activity.

title: Uncle Fester's Ridiculous Paper Trail
description: According to the Season 2 easter egg breakdown, Uncle Fester is carrying 33 driver's licenses and 18 passports, and Fred Armisen actually sat for every single one of those photos so the prop department had real faces to print.

title: Nevermore's Gargoyles Are Basically a Seating Chart
description: Production designer Mark Scruton has explained that the gargoyles carved into Nevermore Academy aren't random, each one was designed to represent a specific outcast group at the school, so you can spot vampires, gorgons and sirens if you look closely at the stonework.

title: The Weathervane Café's Tim Burton Tribute Wall
description: The back wall of the Weathervane Café in Jericho is covered in weathervanes that are easy to miss, but a couple of them are shaped like props from Tim Burton's other films, including one topped with Willy Wonka's hat and another with scissors nodding to Edward Scissorhands.

title: Nevermore's Exterior Is a Real Romanian Castle
description: For Season 1, the outside of Nevermore Academy was Cantacuzino Castle in Bușteni, Romania. It was actually built in 1911 as a summer home for a former Romanian Prime Minister, long before it got a second life as a boarding school for outcasts.

title: Nevermore Packed Up and Moved to Ireland
description: Season 2 swapped Romania for Ireland, with Charleville Castle in County Offaly taking over as the new Nevermore Academy interiors and courtyards, giving the school a slightly different but equally gothic feel.

title: Charleville Castle's Actual Ghost Story
description: The real Charleville Castle used for Season 2's Nevermore is reportedly haunted by the ghost of a young girl named Harriet, who is said to have died in a fall on the property around 160 years ago, which honestly feels almost too on brand for this show.

title: Wednesday Beat Stranger Things' Netflix Record
description: Wednesday's first season racked up 341.2 million hours viewed in a single week, which knocked Stranger Things Season 4 off the top spot for the biggest week ever for an English-language Netflix series.

title: Enid's New Look Was a Cyberpunk Makeover
description: Enid Sinclair's hair gets an update for Season 2, shorter and more intensely coloured than before, and the team behind it has said the new style was deliberately inspired by cyberpunk aesthetics rather than just being a random refresh.

title: 70 Sets, Six Sound Stages, One Season
description: Just to give a sense of the scale involved, Season 1 was built across roughly 70 different sets spread over six sound stages in Bucharest, on top of all the real castles and buildings used for exteriors.

title: Wednesday and Her Principal Are Real-Life Friends
description: Gwendoline Christie, who plays Principal Weems, is a genuine off-screen friend of Jenna Ortega's, which makes their on-screen dynamic even funnier once you know it, especially with Christie towering at 6'3" over Ortega's 5'1".

title: Morticia's Cottage Was Built in an Irish Forest
description: Rotwood Cottage, the place Morticia gets to renovate while acting as Nevermore's gala chair in Season 2, was actually filmed out in the Cloragh Woods of County Wicklow, Ireland.

title: The Psychiatric Facility Was a College
description: Willow Hill, the psychiatric facility holding Tyler in Season 2, was filmed at Clonliffe College in Dublin. The location team picked it specifically because its gothic architecture already looked like it belonged in Wednesday's world without much extra work.

title: Jenna Ortega Got a Seat at the Table for Season 2
description: The Wednesday set has apparently always been a collaborative place, but for Season 2, Jenna Ortega made that official by taking on a producer credit, giving her an actual say in decisions rather than just being the lead actor.

title: Morticia's Cottage Is Full of 60s Show Nods
description: Keep half an eye on the background of Morticia's cottage in Season 2 and you'll catch a stuffed bear, an iron maiden and a taxidermied tortoise, all quiet little references scattered in from the 1964 Addams Family TV series.

title: Frozen Alien in the Ice
description: Right at the start of the game, during the getaway from the Ludendorff bank job, there's a detour off the main road that leads down to a frozen river. Get out and walk to the middle of the ice and you'll find an alien frozen solid beneath the surface, just staring back up at you. You can't hang around admiring it though, since the mission fails if you're out of the car too long.

title: A Second Saucer at the Bottom of the Sea
description: Separate from the sunken submarine and its cash stash, there's an actual crashed UFO resting on the ocean floor near the northern edge of the map. You'll need a submersible or scuba gear to reach it, and the game never explains where it came from, it's just sitting there in the dark, waiting for divers determined enough to find it.

title: Something Big in the Deep
description: Swim far enough out to the eastern edge of the map and you'll come across a colossal skeleton lying on the seabed, way bigger than anything that should logically be down there. Nobody at Rockstar has ever officially confirmed what it's meant to be, so players have spent years guessing whether it's a nod to Moby Dick or just a bit of deep-sea weirdness for its own sake.

title: A Novel by J. Marston
description: Scan enough bookshelves around Los Santos and you'll spot a paperback titled 'Red Dead' credited to an author named J. Marston. It's a cheeky little wink to Red Dead Redemption's John Marston, and fans have long assumed it's meant to be a novel written by his son Jack, tying two of Rockstar's biggest worlds together with nothing more than a book spine.

title: Thelma & Louise Reenacted at Raton Canyon
description: Fly a helicopter over Raton Canyon between roughly 7 and 8pm and, if the timing lines up, you'll catch a car sailing off the cliff edge below, a direct recreation of the famous final scene from the 1991 film Thelma & Louise. It's easy to miss entirely if you're not looking down at exactly the right moment.

title: An X-Files Poster Under the Waves
description: Dive down off the coast near Sandy Shores and among the other underwater oddities you'll find a wrecked plane carrying a poster of a UFO with the words 'accept the truth' printed underneath, a clear riff on the famous 'I Want To Believe' poster that hung in Fox Mulder's office throughout The X-Files.

title: Climbing Inside the Vinewood Sign
description: Los Santos' answer to the Hollywood sign isn't just there to look at from a distance. Players can actually climb up and sit inside the letters themselves, taking in one of the best skyline views the game offers, especially if you time it for the evening when the city lights start coming on below.

title: Fifty Pieces of a Fallen Ship
description: Once Franklin meets the conspiracy theorist Omega, a full collectible hunt opens up for fifty scattered spaceship parts hidden across San Andreas, some tucked into buildings and rooftops, others sitting underwater or buried in tunnels only reachable by helicopter. Omega himself suggests they're wreckage from a UFO that crashed nearby, though the game is careful never to confirm it outright.

title: A Cult Built to Mock Scientology
description: The Epsilon Program, the in-game religion Michael can get roped into, was written as a pointed parody of Scientology and the wider self-help industry, right down to the invented founder Cris Formage and a made-up deity called Kifflom. Everything about the group, from the donation requests to the robes, is playing the con for laughs while still poking fun at very real belief systems.

title: The Fans Who Believed Too Much
description: Former Rockstar writer Lazlow Jones has told the story of getting a genuinely unsettling voicemail while GTA V was in development, from a woman claiming to speak for a real group of players who'd formed their own version of the Epsilon Program after tracing its lore through earlier games. What started as satire of cults had, without Rockstar ever intending it, grown a small real-world following of its own.

title: Three Different Body Clocks
description: Not every protagonist sleeps the same amount. Put Trevor to bed and the clock jumps forward a full twelve hours, Franklin only needs eight, while Michael gets away with just six hours before he's back on his feet. It's a small detail, but it quietly reinforces each character's personality without a single line of dialogue.

title: A Map You Need a Blacklight For
description: The physical map that shipped inside the Special Edition of the game hides an extra layer that only shows up under UV light, revealing a fake business listing for 'Trevor Philips Enterprises' along with a set of driving directions to a spot near Raton Canyon, treasure-map style, for anyone dedicated enough to shine a blacklight over their strategy guide.

title: Wheels Borrowed From Real Showrooms
description: Open up the wheel customisation menu at any Los Santos garage and a surprising number of the designs are lifted straight from real cars. 'Duper 7' matches the Nissan GT-R, 'Lozspeed Mk.V' is the Ferrari 458 Italia's rims, and 'Diamond Cut' comes straight off a pre-facelift Porsche 997 Turbo, small details most players drive right past without ever noticing.

title: Bigger Than Three Games Combined
description: When Rockstar's map for GTA V leaked ahead of launch, fans worked out it clocked in at around 49 square miles, comfortably larger than San Andreas, GTA IV, and Red Dead Redemption's maps added together. For a studio that had been squeezing stories out of the same engine for years, it was a genuinely staggering jump in scale.

title: More Saucers Hiding in Plain Sight
description: The Mount Chiliad mural isn't the whole story. Follow its clues far enough and they point to three more UFO sightings scattered across the map: a saucer hovering over a mural painted by hippies at Salvation Mountain, another looming above Fort Zancudo's military base, and a third that's crash-landed out in the Pacific Ocean, each one just as easy to miss as the last.

title: A Face That Looks a Lot Like Jesse Pinkman
description: On the original release of the game, a spray-painted face is tucked into a rock edge on Mount Chiliad's northern slope, and it bears an uncanny resemblance to Jesse Pinkman from Breaking Bad. It has nothing to do with the Chiliad mural conspiracy and serves no purpose whatsoever, and in the enhanced version of the game it was quietly swapped out for a drawing of a rooster instead.

title: Michael's Path to "Enlightenment"
description: Players who let Michael get drawn into the Epsilon Program can work through a full chain of optional missions, handing over cash, wearing the robes for ten days straight, running miles through the desert, and even stealing cars in the cult's name, all in pursuit of an ending where he finally has to decide whether enlightenment or their money is the real prize.

title: Fifty Scraps of Paper
description: Alongside the spaceship parts, GTA V hides fifty individual letter scraps across Los Santos and Blaine County, wedged behind road signs, on top of construction cranes, inside skate parks, and even balanced on a ping pong table. Collecting the full set unlocks its own separate reward, quietly rewarding players who like to explore every inch of the map.

title: The Alien Egg Nobody Was Meant to Find
description: Buried in GTA V's game files from launch was a glowing alien egg that only third-party trainers could ever spawn, completely unreachable through normal play. Years later, Rockstar brought it back for real in GTA Online's Gunrunning update, hiding it behind an absurdly specific condition: finish 600 resupply missions, then start one more between 9pm and 11pm and hope the game rolls it for you.

title: Dressing Up as Heisenberg
description: It's no coincidence that a middle-aged bank robber turned drug cook shares a few too many biographical beats with Walter White. Rockstar leaned into it further by letting players kit Michael out in the yellow hazmat suit, glasses, and bald cap combo needed to make him look just like Heisenberg himself, a knowing nod dropped right as Breaking Bad's final season was airing.

title: Private Military, Public Punchline
description: Merryweather Security, the ruthless private military contractor that hounds all three protagonists throughout the story, is a clear stand-in for real-world firms like Blackwater. Rockstar leans into the satire hard, giving Merryweather every trapping of a legitimate defence contractor while making it obvious they're just as amoral and trigger-happy as anyone else in Los Santos.

title: The Mr. 7 Scene Oda Forgot He Wrote
description: Showrunner Matt Owens pitched turning a single throwaway manga mention into a full scene, Zoro's backstory duel with a Baroque Works agent called Mr. 7. Oda reportedly turned to his own staff and asked if he'd actually written that, since he had no memory of it and had never even drawn the character.

title: Oda Drew Mr. 7 Overnight
description: Once reminded that he'd mentioned the character in an old fan Q&A session years earlier, Oda went away and came back the very next day with a concept sketch of Mr. 7, which the production then used as the basis for casting and designing the character for the show.

title: Beating Stranger Things Out of the Gate
description: In its opening weekend the show hit number one on Netflix's chart in 84 countries at once, edging out the previous record of 83 that had been shared by Wednesday and Stranger Things Season 4.

title: 18.5 Million Views Before the First Week Was Even Over
description: Netflix's own numbers put the show at 18.5 million views and over 140 million hours watched in just its first four days, outpacing the opening of the streamer's earlier anime adaptation Cowboy Bebop by a wide margin.

title: Renewed for Season 2 Inside Two Weeks
description: Netflix greenlit a second season remarkably fast, with showrunner Matt Owens confirming the renewal in a public message to fans roughly two weeks after the show's premiere, by which point it had already crossed 37.8 million views.

title: A 96% Audience Score That Silenced Doubters
description: Given Netflix's rocky track record with anime adaptations, expectations were shaky going in. The show ended up landing a 96% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes from over ten thousand ratings, one of the highest audience scores any Netflix original had earned at that point.

title: Casting the East Blue's First Villains
description: Jeff Ward, previously known for playing Deke Shaw on Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D., was announced as Buggy the Clown, while McKinley Belcher III, familiar from Ozark, took on the fish-man pirate Arlong, rounding out the early antagonists opposite the Straw Hats.

title: Vincent Regan Trades Troy for the Marines
description: The role of Vice Admiral Garp, Luffy's formidable grandfather, went to Vincent Regan, an actor better known up to that point for big historical epics like Troy and 300.

title: Morgan Davies Plays the Marine Who Starts It All
description: Koby, the timid cabin boy who befriends Luffy in the very first episode and eventually joins the Marines, is played by Morgan Davies, whose earlier credits included the film Storm Boy.

title: A Second Wave of Casting Brought Mihawk and Kaya
description: During a Netflix Geeked Week event, the production revealed Steven Ward as the fearsome swordsman Mihawk and Celeste Loots as Kaya, alongside Langley Kirkwood as Captain Morgan, Alexander Maniatis as Klahadore, Craig Fairbrass as chef Zeff and Chioma Umeala as Nojiko.

title: The Manga Sold Over 460 Million Copies Before the Show Even Aired
description: By the time Netflix announced its live-action cast, Oda's original manga had already sold in excess of 460 million copies worldwide, a scale of popularity that made adapting it into live action feel like an especially high-stakes gamble.

title: The Adaptation Squeezes Five Arcs Into One Season
description: Season 1 condenses the first five arcs of the original story, everything from Luffy leaving home to arriving at the Baratie and beyond, into just eight episodes, which meant plenty of streamlining and merging of side plots along the way.

title: Mini Buggy Makes the Cut
description: Long-time readers know Buggy occasionally reduces his split-apart body parts down to a tiny, doll-sized version of himself for comedic effect. That gag from the manga and anime made it into the live-action too, tucked in as a quick visual joke rather than a major plot beat.

title: A Newspaper-Delivering Seagull
description: Early on, Luffy tries to recruit a bird for his crew that's actually a Newscoo, the seagull species from the manga whose entire job in this world is delivering newspapers and wanted posters between islands.

title: Zoro's Whole Introduction Is an Off-Page Fight, Brought to Life
description: In the manga, Zoro's confrontation with the Baroque Works recruiter was only ever referenced after the fact, never actually drawn or shown happening. The Netflix version stages the whole thing as an on-screen fight, giving fans their first ever look at a moment that had existed only in text for over two decades.

title: Mr. 7's Successor Was Already Waiting in the Wings
description: In the wider story, the numbered Baroque Works agent titles don't retire when someone dies, they just get reassigned. After Zoro kills the original Mr. 7, the position and number are picked up by a new operative who later appears working alongside Miss Father's Day during the Arabasta arc.

title: Ilia Isorelýs Paulino Steps Into Alvida's Boots
description: The role of Iron Mace Alvida, the vain pirate captain who terrorizes Koby before Luffy shows up, went to Ilia Isorelýs Paulino, an actress previously seen in Queenpins and The Sex Lives of College Girls.

title: Aidan Scott's Helmeppo Gets a Redemption Arc
description: Aidan Scott plays Helmeppo, the spoiled son of a corrupt Marine captain who starts the show as a straightforward antagonist. The character's live-action arc follows the manga in gradually softening him, with Garp and Koby ending up shaping him into someone more sympathetic by the season's end.

title: One Piece Broke What Fans Called Hollywood's Anime Curse
description: After a string of poorly received anime-to-live-action adaptations, including Netflix's own Cowboy Bebop and Death Note, One Piece was widely credited by critics and fans as the first Hollywood adaptation to genuinely land, both narratively and with its casting.

title: 10 Million Views and Still Climbing in Week Three
description: The show wasn't just a one-week wonder, it held the number one spot on Netflix's television chart for three consecutive weeks, pulling in another 10 million views in that third week alone after topping 19 million the week before.

title: A Facebook Parody With Teeth
description: LifeInvader, the social network Michael's crew has to hack early in the story, is Rockstar's answer to Facebook, right down to its founder Jay Norris being dogged by accusations that he stole the whole idea from a friend, a none-too-subtle poke at the real controversy that's followed Mark Zuckerberg for years.

title: Fruit, Bleeter, and the Rest of Silicon Valley
description: LifeInvader wasn't the only tech giant Rockstar decided to skewer. Fruit Computers stands in for Apple, complete with its own late founder who's clearly meant to evoke Steve Jobs, while Bleeter fills the Twitter-shaped hole, giving Los Santos its own fully formed, thoroughly mocked version of the modern internet.

title: A Fake Website That Outlived Its Marketing Campaign
description: Rockstar didn't just build LifeInvader as an in-game joke, they actually launched Lifeinvader.com as a working promotional site just before release, complete with browsable fake profiles and brand tie-ins. It stuck around online for a full decade before Rockstar finally shut it down, quietly redirecting visitors to the main GTA portal instead.

title: Danny Brown's Cameo Before He Got His Own Station
description: Years before rapper Danny Brown got his own dedicated station added to the game, he'd already snuck into GTA V in a much smaller way, voicing a random NPC hanging around the Los Santos beachfront who reacts in his own voice if players decide to mess with him.

title: The Composer From Drive Gets His Own Station
description: French artist Kavinsky, best known for scoring much of the synth-heavy soundtrack to the film Drive, hosts his own in-universe station called NightRide FM. It's a neat bit of cross-pollination, especially given GTA V already hides a separate visual nod to Drive in one of its clothing stores.

title: Real Musicians Curating Fictional Airwaves
description: At launch, several of the game's radio stations were personally curated and hosted by real musicians rather than voice actors playing a character. Flying Lotus, Bootsy Collins, and Frank Ocean all lent their names and their taste in music to specific stations, giving Los Santos' airwaves a level of authenticity most game soundtracks don't bother with.

title: The Radio Voice Who Became a Character
description: Lazlow Jones has voiced a radio personality in every mainline GTA game since the third entry and has been the series' chief writer for its radio content behind the scenes for just as long. GTA V finally gave him a physical, on-screen role too, one where the protagonists get to put him through some fairly humiliating situations for a change.

title: Three Ways to End It, One Official Answer
description: Franklin's final choice lets players kill Trevor, kill Michael, or talk the whole crew into fighting their enemies together instead. For over a decade Rockstar left it ambiguous which ending actually 'happened', with fans piecing together clues from GTA Online, until a later in-game update finally confirmed once and for all that the option where everybody lives is the canon outcome.

title: A Real App for a Fictional Dog
description: Franklin's rottweiler Chop wasn't just a background character, Rockstar built an actual companion app called iFruit that let players feed him, walk him, and teach him tricks Tamagotchi-style from their phone. Keep him happy enough in the app and he'd actually behave better and sniff out collectibles more reliably back in the main game.

title: A Meth Lab Above the Liquor Store
description: Trevor's entire meth operation is run out of the upper floor of a run-down liquor store called Ace Liquor in Sandy Shores, with the shop itself acting as a front and headquarters for Trevor Philips Enterprises long before the main story even kicks off, quietly establishing his criminal empire before players ever set foot inside.

title: Beverly Hills, Rebuilt as Rockford Hills
description: Michael's mansion sits in Rockford Hills, the game's stand-in for the real Beverly Hills, complete with its own version of Rodeo Drive renamed Portola Drive. It's one of dozens of Los Santos neighbourhoods built as a direct, slightly exaggerated mirror of an actual LA district, right down to the shopping.

title: A Concert Venue Carved Into the Hills
description: The Vinewood Bowl, where the in-game reality show Fame or Shame gets filmed, is modeled closely on the real Hollywood Bowl, sharing the same distinctive concave, bowl-shaped hillside the venue is named after. It's a small detail, but it's exactly the kind of one-to-one landmark swap Rockstar loves hiding throughout the map.

title: Netflix Rescued It From Cancellation
description: You actually started life on Lifetime back in 2018 and flopped hard enough that the network dropped it after one season. Netflix had only bought the international rights at first, but once they saw how the show performed on their platform they bought it outright and turned it into a full-blown Netflix Original. Producer Greg Berlanti has said it went from one of the least-watched shows of his career to the most-watched almost overnight.

title: Penn Badgley Nearly Said No to Joe
description: Penn Badgley wasn't sold on playing Joe Goldberg when the part first came his way. He's talked about feeling genuinely conflicted, worried that the show would end up romanticising a killer instead of exposing him. It was long conversations with creators Greg Berlanti and Sera Gamble about Joe's psychology that finally talked him into it.

title: Victoria Pedretti Auditioned for Beck First
description: Before she ever played Love Quinn, Victoria Pedretti tried out for the role of Beck in season one and even got a callback. She didn't land it, but she's said she's glad it worked out that way since it freed her up to do The Haunting of Hill House, which is what eventually brought her back into Sera Gamble and Greg Berlanti's orbit for Love.

title: Dylan Arnold Auditioned Three Times
description: Theo actor Dylan Arnold has one of the funniest audition histories on the show. He first read for Joe in season one, then came back to try out for Forty in season two, and only landed a part on his third attempt when he was cast as Theo in season three. He even went to college with Elizabeth Lail, who played Beck.

title: The Blood Is Basically Syrup
description: All the gruesome bloodshed in You comes from a sticky homemade mix of sugar and red food dye that gets pumped through rigged machines. Victoria Pedretti has described filming those scenes as feeling weirdly mechanical rather than emotional, partly because the crew sometimes had to stop and fix a blood machine that wasn't spraying correctly.

title: A Prosthetic Arm for the Finger Scene
description: When Jasper cuts off Joe's finger in season two, that wasn't Penn Badgley's real arm on screen. He wore a prosthetic limb built specifically so it could be sliced open convincingly for the camera, letting the effects team get the gory shot without anyone actually losing a finger.

title: A Body Made From Real Human Hair
description: For the meat grinder scene in season two, the production built a full-sized prosthetic corpse so lifelike it unsettled Penn Badgley to even touch it. Every strand of body hair on the dummy was individually applied real human hair, and the whole thing was rigged to bleed once the effects team started cutting into it.

title: Joe and Forty's Scene Was Partly Improvised
description: James Scully has revealed that a key emotional moment between Forty and Joe in season two wasn't fully scripted. He and Penn Badgley talked at length about the strange, intense bond between the two characters and built part of the scene themselves, aiming for something intimate that wasn't romantic or violent, just two men being unusually honest with each other.

title: Paco Doesn't Exist in the Books
description: Sweet, troubled Paco and his mum Claudia were invented purely for the TV adaptation. Showrunner Sera Gamble has said Paco exists to show Joe's gentler, more protective side, feeding him, keeping him out of trouble, teaching him to read. It makes his betrayal at the end of season one, when he lets Beck's escape attempt fail, land even harder.

title: Ellie Was Created for the Show
description: Fan favourite Ellie, Delilah's teenage sister, doesn't appear anywhere in Caroline Kepnes' novels. The writers added her to give Joe a relationship that felt uncomplicated and almost paternal for once, which makes it all the more unsettling once his usual manipulative streak starts creeping into it.

title: Natalie Never Appears in the Novels
description: Joe's ill-fated neighbour Natalie in season two is a TV-only invention. Because the show diverged so far from the ending of the Hidden Bodies novel, the writers needed a fresh obsession for Joe once he landed in Madre Linda, and Natalie filled that gap instead of the librarian character from the books.

title: Marienne Is a Reworked Book Character
description: Marienne isn't a straight adaptation of anyone from the third novel, You Love Me. She's loosely built from a librarian character named Mary Kay, though the show changes her daughter's age and softens how serious her relationship with Joe becomes compared to the source material.

title: Book Three Sends Joe Somewhere Totally Different
description: The You Love Me novel takes Joe's story in a very different direction than season three. In the book he's just out of prison and relocates to Bainbridge Island in Washington after the Quinn family pays him off, splitting from Love entirely rather than raising baby Henry with her in the suburbs.

title: Love Isn't a Killer in the Books
description: The season two twist where Love reveals she's murdered people too doesn't exist in Kepnes' novels. Book Love never kills anyone. When she learns about Joe's past there, she simply chooses to stay with him out of love rather than confessing a body count of her own.

title: Candace's Fate Changes Between Book and Show
description: In the original novel there's no ambiguity about what happens to Candace, Joe drowns her at Brighton Beach and that's that. The show's writers deliberately left it open, having her turn up alive at the very end of season one so the story could go somewhere the book readers wouldn't expect.

title: Candace's Alias Comes From the Sequel Novel
description: When Candace resurfaces in season two under the name Amy Adam, that's actually a nod to Hidden Bodies. A character called Amy Adam shows up in the book too, and it's the reason Joe heads to Los Angeles in the first place, chasing her down after she robs the bookstore.

title: Peach's Wardrobe Was Shay Mitchell's Own Clothes
description: A lot of Peach Salinger's very specific, moneyed style in season one came straight from Shay Mitchell's personal closet. She's said she loved getting to dress up after years of a stripped-back look on Pretty Little Liars, and even brought extra bags of her own clothes to set to work out Peach's look with the costume team.

title: Mooney's Bookstore Is a Real Manhattan Shop
description: The bookstore where Joe works isn't a set built from scratch, it's Logos Bookstore on Manhattan's Upper East Side, used for both the exterior and interior shots. Fans do occasionally stop by hoping for a peek at the infamous glass cage in the basement, but that part, thankfully, was never real.

title: Season Three Shares a Backlot With Gilmore Girls
description: Most of season three was shot on the Warner Bros backlot rather than on location, the same one used for Gilmore Girls and Pretty Little Liars. Love's bakery, A Fresh Tart, sits on the same street set as Luke's Diner, just around the corner, and the backlot is open for public tours if you want to spot it yourself.

title: Someone Else Reads Joe's Voiceover on Set
description: Penn Badgley barely speaks out loud while filming most of his scenes, since Joe's constant internal narration gets recorded separately afterward. On set, his stand-in reads those inner-monologue lines off camera so Penn can react in the moment, then Penn records the actual voiceover later in a booth.

title: Penn Badgley Compared Joe to Dan Humphrey
description: Penn Badgley has openly connected Joe Goldberg to his old Gossip Girl character Dan Humphrey, calling Joe a warped version of what Dan might have become. He's pointed out that Dan always saw himself as an outsider looking in on privilege, when in reality he was already firmly on the inside the whole time.

title: The Word 'You' Gets Said Nearly 4,000 Times
description: Netflix actually crunched the numbers on this one. Across just the first two seasons, the word 'you' is spoken 3,857 times, largely thanks to Joe's endless second-person inner monologues aimed at whoever he's currently fixated on. Season one alone accounts for 241 uses in the opening run of episodes.

title: Actors Got Certified to Film on Subway Tracks
description: For the season one scene where Beck falls onto the subway tracks and Joe jumps down after her, Elizabeth Lail and Penn Badgley had to complete an eight-hour MTA safety course beforehand. They came away with real transit cards certifying them to legally be down on the tracks, essentially the same training given to trainee train conductors.

title: You Was Originally Written for Showtime
description: Before Lifetime picked it up, You was actually developed with Showtime in mind. Showrunner Sera Gamble has said the earliest draft just didn't line up with Showtime's vision for the show, and that Lifetime ended up being a better creative fit despite it not being the obvious home for a story this dark.

title: Season Five Brought Joe Back to Where It Started
description: The final season deliberately loops back to New York, with key scenes shot around Central Park, Tavern on the Green and the Bleecker Street subway station, the same borough where Joe's very first obsession began. Production even filmed a sequence at the old Joliet Prison in Illinois, using the crumbling building as a stand-in for Joe finally facing his past.

title: Almost a Movie, Almost Lindsay Lohan
description: Before it was ever a TV show, Gossip Girl was being kicked around as a one-off feature film, and the name attached to play Blair Waldorf at one point was Lindsay Lohan. Wild to picture now given how synonymous Leighton Meester became with the role.

title: Jennifer Lawrence Tried Out for Serena
description: Long before she was an Oscar winner, Jennifer Lawrence actually auditioned for the role of Serena van der Woodsen. The part obviously went to Blake Lively, but it's a fun bit of what-could-have-been casting trivia.

title: Blair's Actress Auditioned for Serena First
description: Leighton Meester is naturally blonde, and her first audition for the show was actually for Serena, not Blair. Producers liked her but felt she suited Blair better, so she dyed her hair brunette on the spot because she wanted the part that badly.

title: Serena and Dan Were Childhood Classmates in Real Life
description: Blake Lively and Penn Badgley didn't meet on set like most people assume. They were actually homeschooled together as kids, and their real-life romance picked back up once they were both cast on the show playing Serena and Dan.

title: Chuck and Nate Were Actually Roommates
description: Ed Westwick and Chace Crawford, who played on-screen frenemies Chuck and Nate, shared a two-bedroom flat in Chelsea while filming. They first bonded at an Arctic Monkeys gig, and by most accounts Crawford eventually moved out because Westwick was too messy to live with.

title: Chuck Bass Changed How Men Dressed
description: Costume designer Eric Daman has said Ed Westwick's polished, suited-up look as Chuck Bass had a genuine influence on menswear at the time, pushing back against the era's more casual, 'Jersey Shore' style of dressing.

title: The Show Turned Bad Reviews Into Adverts
description: Rather than being embarrassed by criticism calling the show inappropriate, the marketing team leaned right into it for season two promos, plastering lines like 'mind-blowingly inappropriate' and 'every parent's nightmare' straight from critics onto the ads.

title: Serena and Dan's Real Breakup Stayed Secret for Months
description: Blake Lively and Penn Badgley dated for around three years while filming, and when they split in 2010 they kept it so quiet that even the crew didn't find out until months later, on the set of the season two finale.

title: Blake Lively's DiCaprio Romance Shaped the Show
description: When Blake Lively started dating Leonardo DiCaprio, the writers apparently drew on it for the show, even shifting filming out to L.A. for a stretch. Writer Joshua Safran later said watching Lively document her life in photos, pre-Instagram, was ahead of its time.

title: The Show Had Its Own Real-Life Script Leaker
description: For a while, scripts kept mysteriously turning up online before episodes aired. Producers hired a private investigator and eventually traced it to a teenage hacker overseas who'd broken into a writer's email and was selling scripts on eBay. Because the hacker was a minor, nothing could be done, so the crew started printing scripts on red paper just to stop leaks.

title: Chuck Bass Never Learned Who Gossip Girl Was
description: Even after starring in the finale where the mystery blogger's identity gets revealed, Ed Westwick has admitted he genuinely still isn't sure who Gossip Girl actually was.

title: New York Had an Official Gossip Girl Day
description: Then-Mayor Michael Bloomberg was such a fan of the show and its effect on the city's image that he officially declared January 26th 'Gossip Girl Day' in New York, and he even popped up with a small cameo in one of the later seasons.

title: Penn Badgley Is Named After a Tennis Ball Brand
description: A random bit of trivia that always gets a laugh: Penn Badgley's first name reportedly comes from the tennis ball company Penn, not any family name or tradition.

title: The Pilot Almost Gave Away Dan Immediately
description: There was a scene cut from the original pilot where Dan's writing habits made test audiences immediately assume he was Gossip Girl. The show pulled that scene so the mystery could actually run for six seasons instead of getting solved in episode one.

title: Born Out of The O.C.'s Success
description: Creators Josh Schwartz and Stephanie Savage had just wrapped up their run on The O.C. and wanted to bring what they'd learned to a New York setting. That itch to do something bigger and glossier in Manhattan is basically where Gossip Girl was born.

title: Chuck's Hotel Is a Real Place You Can Book
description: The Empire Hotel, which Chuck Bass owns on the show, is an actual working hotel in New York. Fans started showing up in droves after it aired, so the bar there began serving Gossip Girl-themed cocktails, including a secret-recipe 'XOXO' drink.

title: Dan Wasn't Always the Top Suspect
description: Writer Joshua Safran has said that his original top picks for the person behind Gossip Girl weren't Dan at all, they were Serena's brother Eric van der Woodsen or her on-off love interest Nate Archibald. Safran left the show before the final season aired, so the reveal that eventually landed wasn't the one he'd been building toward.

title: Dorota's Actress Thinks She Should Have Been Gossip Girl
description: Zuzanna Szadkowski, who played the Waldorf family's maid Dorota, said in an interview that she genuinely believes her character would have made a better final reveal than Dan. A lot of fans who found the actual ending underwhelming tend to agree with her.

title: The Met Steps Were the Group's Unofficial Meeting Spot
description: Throughout the series, whenever the core group needed to gather for something big, they always seemed to end up at the Metropolitan Museum steps, and that's exactly where the whole cast reconvenes right before the finale's big reveals.

title: You Never Actually See Gossip Girl's Face, Just Hear Her
description: For all six seasons, the anonymous voice narrating everyone's scandals belonged to Kristen Bell, who never appeared on screen and was never credited as a main cast member despite basically being the show's guiding presence.

title: The Whole Thing Started With a Book Packager
description: Author Cecily von Ziegesar dreamed up the Gossip Girl world while working a day job at Alloy Entertainment, a book-packaging company. The novels hit the top of the New York Times bestseller list back in 2002, a full five years before the TV show ever aired.

title: Blair's School Is Based on the Author's Real One
description: Constance Billard, the fictional private school Blair and Serena attend, is a exaggerated stand-in for Nightingale-Bamford, the real Manhattan school Cecily von Ziegesar herself attended as a teenager. A lot of the show's rich-kid drama was apparently pulled straight from her own school days.

title: Charlie Don't Surf Is an Apocalypse Now Line
description: The Saudi Arabia invasion mission borrows its name straight from Apocalypse Now, where Robert Duvall's Kilgore snarls the same line before an airstrike. Infinity Ward leaned on war-movie references a lot for mission titles, and this is one of the more obvious ones once you know it.

title: Death From Above Basically Wrote the Rulebook
description: Handing the player a gunship, a thermal camera, and a group of ground troops to protect turned out to be such a good formula that other studios copied it wholesale. Ace Combat: Assault Horizon's own AC-130 level lifts the structure so closely, right down to the three weapon types, that critics called it out directly.

title: The AC-130 Was Nearly a Multiplayer Vehicle
description: Leftover game files reference multiplayer versions of the AC-130's 25mm, 40mm, and 105mm guns, suggesting the gunship was at one point planned as a killstreak-style reward you could call in online. It got cut before launch and wouldn't actually show up as a multiplayer reward until Modern Warfare 2.

title: All Ghillied Up Owes a Debt to Behind Enemy Lines
description: The whole atmosphere of the mission, two operatives creeping through hostile, war-torn territory, mirrors the Owen Wilson film Behind Enemy Lines pretty closely. There's even a specific beat, a huge convoy cresting a grassy hill toward the player, that plays almost shot-for-shot like a scene from the movie.

title: The Ghost Town Line Belongs to MacMillan, Not Price
description: One of the most quoted lines from the whole game, 'Fifty thousand people used to live here. Now it's a ghost town,' actually comes from Captain MacMillan surveying Pripyat, not Captain Price like a lot of players remember it. It's a small mix-up that's stuck around in fan trivia for years.

title: Silence Gets Its Own Reward
description: Finish All Ghillied Up from start to finish without a single enemy ever noticing you and you'll unlock the achievement Ghillies in the Mist, a nice nod to how tense and deliberate that mission is built to feel.

title: You Can Blow Your Cover on Purpose
description: The stealth mission technically lets you go loud if you fancy it. Shoot down the enemy helicopter patrolling overhead with a Stinger and, in the remastered version at least, you actually get an achievement for it rather than being punished for breaking stealth.

title: Swapping Weapons Confuses the Next Mission
description: There's a funny little inventory quirk in the original release: trade your USP .45 for something like an RPG-7 or a P90 during All Ghillied Up and the next mission hands you an AK-47 out of nowhere instead of what you'd actually earned. It got quietly fixed when the remaster came out.

title: It Was the Best-Selling Game of Its Entire Year
description: By January 2008, Activision was able to say Call of Duty 4 had sold over seven million copies worldwide and was officially the number one title across every format for all of 2007, based on combined NPD, Chart-Track and GfK data.

title: It Swept Its Own Awards Show
description: At the 11th Annual Interactive Achievement Awards, the game didn't just take home Overall Game of the Year, it also picked up Console Game of the Year, Action Game of the Year, and Outstanding Achievement in Online Gameplay in the same night.

title: It Crossed Ten Million Copies Within a Year
description: Studio head Vince Zampella confirmed to press that the game had passed 10 million copies sold worldwide, with the Xbox 360 version pulling ahead as the top-selling platform, not bad for a game that had launched barely a year earlier.

title: The Achievement List Is Basically One Long Pun
description: Protecting the Abrams tank named War Pig gets you 'Save the Bacon.' Cutting the power gets you 'Dancing in the Dark.' Carrying an injured MacMillan gets you 'Piggyback Ride.' Whoever wrote the achievement names was clearly having fun with it.

title: The Rescued Tank Has an Actual Name
description: The M1A1 Abrams your squad frees during The Bog isn't just 'the tank,' it's nicknamed War Pig, and that nickname goes on to become the title of the mission right after.

title: Death From Above Picks Up Mid-Sentence
description: The gunship mission doesn't start cold. It's a direct continuation of Hunted, where Price's helicopter gets shot down and the squad has to survive on foot until an AC-130 shows up to save them, at which point the player takes over as the gunship's own operator. It's a smoother handoff between missions than most shooters bothered with at the time.

title: Gaz Set a Training Record You're Meant to Chase
description: During the F.N.G. training level, Gaz holds a squad record of 19 seconds on the obstacle course. Beating it isn't required to progress, but it is tied to an achievement, so plenty of players have spent way too long trying to shave off a second or two.

title: Stick Around After the Credits for a Rap Track
description: If you let the credits roll all the way through the first song, someone introduces a rap track that name-drops both Call of Duty 2 and Call of Duty 4, a little bonus most players never sit through long enough to catch.

title: The Flashback Mission Is Technically Out of Order
description: All Ghillied Up is the thirteenth level you actually play, but story-wise it's the very first thing that happens in the whole game, set a full decade before the rest of the campaign. It's an unusual structural choice for an FPS campaign of that era.

title: There's an Achievement for Ruining a Propaganda Broadcast
description: During Charlie Don't Surf, Al-Asad's speech plays on a bank of TVs scattered around the level. Shoot every single one out and you're rewarded with the achievement Your Show Sucks, which might be the pettiest achievement name in the whole game.

title: One Achievement Is Just Straightforwardly Dark
description: No Rest for the Weary asks you to stab a wounded, crawling enemy rather than just leaving them be. It's a grim little piece of dark humour hidden in the achievement list.

title: Saving One Trapped Marine Gets Its Own Name
description: Amid the chaos of War Pig, there's a specific trapped soldier called Private Roycewicz stuck on a staircase. Rescuing him specifically is tied to the achievement Rescue Roycewicz, a nice bit of care put into a background character most players would otherwise never notice by name.

title: The Gunship's Three Guns All Behave Differently
description: In Death From Above, the AC-130's 105mm cannon has a huge blast radius but a painfully long reload, the 40mm Bofors auto-cannon is fully automatic with a medium splash area, and the 25mm Gatling guns trade splash damage for the tightest zoom, useful for picking off targets right next to friendly troops without hitting them.

title: There's a Reward for a Perfect Gunship Shot
description: Land a single 105mm round in just the right spot during Death From Above and take out five enemies at once, and you'll pick up the achievement Straight Flush, a small but satisfying nod to how brutal that cannon can be when it lines up right.

title: The Spidey-Sense That Foreshadows a Different Fate
description: Pay attention to the colours around Miles' head the very first time his spidey-sense kicks in - they're purple and green. Once Peter B. Parker finishes training him, that shifts to the usual red and blue. Purple and green just happen to be Prowler's colours, which lines up nicely with the Earth-42 ending where an un-bitten Miles becomes the Prowler instead of Spider-Man.

title: A Stamp of Approval From a Long-Dead Censor
description: Right after the studio logos, the film flashes the old Comics Code Authority seal, a real stamp that used to appear on comics to reassure parents the content was tame. It was officially retired back in 2011, so bringing it back here is a sly little wink, especially since Spider-Man 2099 spends the movie acting like a one-man censorship board trying to keep Miles in line.

title: Donald Glover's Full-Circle Prowler Cameo
description: Donald Glover pops up voicing a captured Prowler, and it's a genuinely lovely bit of history repeating itself. Glover played Aaron Davis (Miles' uncle) in Homecoming, and years before that he famously campaigned to play Spider-Man himself, even wearing Spidey pyjamas in an episode of Community. Miles Morales was partly inspired by that campaign, so seeing Glover finally show up in a spider-suit, even a villainous one, feels like the story closing a loop.

title: The Bag-Headed Spider-Man Cameo
description: Among the sea of Spider-People wandering around headquarters is one wearing a paper bag over his head with a Fantastic Four costume underneath. That's a direct pull from an old comic run where Peter lost his suit and had to improvise, earning him the nickname Bombastic Bag-Man. Blink and you'll miss him, but it's exactly the kind of deep-cut reference the movie is stuffed with.

title: A News Report That Teases the Next Villain Team
description: During the Earth-42 sequence, a background newscast mentions something called the Sinister Six Cartel running the city, and the signage around suggests Electro, Vulture, Sandman, Scorpion, Doc Ock and Rhino are all in on it. It's a throwaway detail on first watch, but it strongly hints at what a version of Miles might have to deal with down the line on that alternate earth.

title: Miguel Name-Drops the MCU's Messiest Spell
description: Miguel O'Hara grumbles about the chaos he's had to clean up thanks to Doctor Strange messing around on Earth-199999, a direct callback to the multiverse-cracking spell from No Way Home. It's a small line, but it confirms the events of that film are part of the Spider-Verse's shared canon, at least from Miguel's exhausted point of view.

title: Six Universes, Six Completely Different Art Styles
description: Producer Phil Lord told Empire that where the first film leaned on one dominant animation style, this sequel juggles six of them. The idea was to make every new universe feel like it was hand-drawn by a completely different artist, so the visuals actually carry the emotion of wherever Miles has landed rather than just looking impressive for its own sake.

title: Mumbattan Is Built From Indian Comic Book Art
description: The Earth-50101 setting, nicknamed Mumbattan, was deliberately designed to echo the look of Indian comic art, and it's the home turf of Pavitr Prabhakar, the Indian Spider-Man who first appeared in a mini-series back in 2004 before being folded into the wider Spider-Verse comics.

title: Nueva York Borrows From Retro-Future Concept Art
description: Spider-Man 2099's home turf, Nueva York, was styled after Syd Mead's illustrations, the same kind of sleek, glassy futurism Mead brought to films like Blade Runner. It gives Miguel's world a cold, almost sterile beauty that fits his buttoned-up, rules-first personality.

title: Gwen's World Is Painted, Not Drawn
description: Earth-65, Gwen Stacy's dimension, uses a watercolour-wash technique meant to mirror the covers of her own comic run, and the colours in her world visibly shift depending on her mood, which is a detail a lot of people don't clock until a rewatch.

title: Miguel's Backhanded Compliment to Lego Peter
description: Somewhere in the Spider-Society crowd is a Lego minifigure version of Spider-Man, and Miguel actually pauses to tell him he's one of the best, brick pun very much intended. It's a throwaway gag, but the animators clearly had fun giving the Lego universe its own little moment in the spotlight.

title: Roughly 280 Spider-People Show Up on Screen
description: The Spider-Society scenes are absolutely rammed with alternate Spider-heroes, somewhere around 280 of them by most counts, though only about a third actually get a name and a line of dialogue. The rest are just background gags for eagle-eyed fans to freeze-frame and argue about online.

title: A Sneaky Nod to Spider-Ham's Pocket Dimension
description: When the Renaissance-Vulture loses a wing mid-fight, she simply pulls a fresh one out of thin air, and Spider-Man 2099 dryly calls it hammerspace. That's a cartoon-logic term, and it's also a cheeky reference to Spider-Ham's whole running gag from the first film of yanking props out of nowhere.

title: A Vulture Straight Out of the Italian Renaissance
description: The Vulture that ambushes Gwen isn't Michael Keaton's version, it's an alternate Adrian Toomes from a dimension stuck in Renaissance-era Italy, complete with Da Vinci-inspired flying contraptions instead of tech-suit wings. It's a fun way to show how differently the same villain can turn out depending on the world he grew up in.

title: One Actor, a Dozen Different Jonahs
description: J.K. Simmons comes back as J. Jonah Jameson, and true to the multiverse setup, we hear versions of him pop up across several different realities. It's a nice bit of continuity fan-service, treating him as the one constant no matter which universe Miles happens to swing through.

title: Cameos From Spider-Man's Cartoon History
description: Keep an eye out during the Spider-Society crowd scenes and you'll spot the lead from the Spectacular Spider-Man animated series delivering a line of encouragement to Miles, along with a version of the 1967 cartoon Spider-Man who swings in, takes a swing, and immediately complains about pulling a muscle.

title: One of the Longest Western Animated Films Ever Made
description: At around two hours and twenty minutes, this is genuinely one of the lengthiest animated films to come out of a major Western studio. Producer Amy Pascal has said the goal was never to just make things bigger for the sake of it, the extra runtime was there to actually earn the audience's investment in the characters.

title: A Modest Budget for a Visually Massive Film
description: For a film with six different animation styles running simultaneously, the reported production budget of around $100 million is surprisingly restrained compared to what major studios usually spend on animated blockbusters. It ended up pulling in close to $691 million worldwide, making it one of the most profitable films of its year.

title: A Record-Setting Opening Weekend
description: The film opened to roughly $120.5 million domestically, more than tripling the opening of the first Into the Spider-Verse. At the time, it stood as one of the biggest debuts of the year for any animated sequel, comfortably outpacing plenty of live-action blockbusters released that same summer.

title: A Blink-and-Miss-It Raimi Trilogy Tribute
description: During a moment about loss shaping the different Spider-heroes, a still frame from Sam Raimi's 2002 film flashes by, including the iconic upside-down kiss between Tobey Maguire and Kirsten Dunst. Over twenty years on, it's still instantly recognisable even hidden in a busy background montage.

title: Alfred Molina's Doc Ock Voice Makes a Return
description: Tucked into the Spider-Society's endless background noise is a voice line lifted from Alfred Molina's Doc Ock in No Way Home, reused here as just another piece of multiverse chatter. It's the kind of thing you'd only catch with subtitles on or a very good pair of headphones.

title: An Into the Spider-Verse Soundbite Gets Reused
description: After the museum fight, listen closely and you'll catch a snippet of Post Malone's voice being replayed, the same audio clip that featured on the soundtrack of the first film. It's a subtle audio callback rather than a visual one, easy to miss if you're not paying attention to the sound design.

title: Difficult Production Conditions Behind the Scenes
description: Reports emerged that the demanding schedule and working conditions on the film led to a wave of animators leaving the production, over a hundred by some accounts. It's a sobering counterpoint to the film's celebrated visuals, and it fed into wider industry conversations about crunch culture in animation.

title: Spielberg Nearly Took the Helm
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: Long before Gore Verbinski signed on, the script did the rounds in the early 90s and actually landed on Steven Spielberg's desk. His take on it wasn't quite what Disney wanted, but he'd apparently floated Bill Murray, Steve Martin, or even Robin Williams to play a version of Jack Sparrow. Wild to think how different the whole franchise could've looked.

title: Verbinski Wanted It Scary AND Funny
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: Gore Verbinski has said the reason he took the job was down to childhood memories of the Disneyland ride, which somehow managed to spook him and make him laugh at the same time. He deliberately chased that exact same tone for the movie, which is why you get walking skeletons in the same film as a permanently sloshed lead character.

title: De Niro Turned Down Jack Sparrow
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: Robert De Niro was reportedly offered the role of Jack Sparrow ahead of Jim Carrey, but passed because he was convinced pirate movies were box office poison. When the film went on to make hundreds of millions, he took a role in Stardust instead, chasing that same swashbuckling fantasy lightning. It didn't strike twice.

title: Jack Sparrow Was Built From a Rock Star and a Skunk
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: Depp has explained that his whole approach to Jack came from treating pirates like the rock stars of their era, so he leaned hard on Keith Richards for the swagger, then mixed in the flouncy, lovestruck energy of Pepe Le Pew for good measure. It's a genuinely bizarre combo on paper that somehow just works on screen.

title: Barbossa's Whole Personality Was in the Hat
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: Geoffrey Rush has said he didn't need to do much soul-searching to find Barbossa's character — the moment he put the hat on, the arrogance and theatrical flourish just came naturally. He's joked the feather alone told him everything about the man's ego.

title: The Rubber Hat Problem
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: Depp's leather hat kept getting knocked or thrown into the ocean during shoots, and after they'd lost around ten of them, costume designer Penny Rose gave up and had a rubber version made instead, purely because it would actually float. Practical problem solving, pirate-movie style.

title: Elizabeth's Cleavage Wasn't Real
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: Keira Knightley was only 17 when she made this and has said her bust looks noticeably bigger in the film than in real life because it was, in her words, literally painted on with makeup. She's talked about it since as just one of those strange, slightly uncomfortable things that used to be considered normal on a big studio shoot.

title: Knightley Was Convinced It Would Bomb
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: According to director Richard Curtis, while Keira Knightley was filming her small role in Love Actually she mentioned she'd just signed on to a pirate movie and flatly said she didn't think it would work, because pirate films always flop. She wasn't exactly wrong about the genre's track record up to that point — just wrong about this particular film.

title: Jack Davenport Had to Be Talked Into It
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: Jack Davenport, who played Commodore Norrington, has admitted he was never a fan of pirate movies growing up and didn't rate the recent ones much either. It was reportedly Verbinski's pitch that this could be the first genuinely good pirate film in fifty years that finally won him over.

title: Zoe Saldana Struggled on Set
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: Long before Avatar and Guardians of the Galaxy, Zoe Saldana played crew member Anamaria in this film, and she's since said the experience wasn't a good one. She's described feeling completely overwhelmed by the scale of a major studio production, the shifting locations, and the pace, and has said she walked away not having enjoyed it much at all — which probably explains why her character never returned for the sequels.

title: The Studio Boss Nearly Killed the Movie
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
