description: Then-Disney CEO Michael Eisner was reportedly never sold on this project. He worried the PG-13 rating would scare off Disney's usual family audience and thought teenagers would see a movie based on a theme park ride as embarrassingly uncool. At more than one point during production he was ready to pull the plug entirely.

title: It Was Almost a Straight-to-DVD Movie
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: Before it became one of the biggest films of 2003, this was originally planned as a direct-to-DVD release, the kind of treatment Disney usually reserved for cheap animated sequels. That's how little confidence the studio initially had in the whole idea.

title: Jack Sparrow Almost Played It Straight
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: The earliest concept for the character was a much more standard swashbuckling hero, with Hugh Jackman apparently in the mix at one stage. It was Depp who pushed the performance into stranger, funnier territory, and while the studio was reportedly baffled by his choices at first, they let him run with it.

title: A Set Fire Nearly Derailed Everything
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: Before principal photography even started, a fire tore through one of the sets in September 2002, racking up hundreds of thousands of dollars in damage. Thankfully nobody was hurt, but it was a rocky start to an already nervous production.

title: Keira Knightley Got Stranded on a Reef
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: During a night shoot, Keira Knightley and her mother, who had to be on set with her since she was a minor, ended up marooned on a reef for close to an hour before anyone could get them off it. Locals had apparently warned the crew that night shoots out there were a bad idea.

title: The Whole Crew Got Seasick
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: Shooting for weeks on the open water off St. Vincent left a huge chunk of the cast and crew seasick, and the medication they took to cope came with its own price: it knocked people out with drowsiness, which slowed filming down even further on an already tight schedule.

title: Verbinski Was Still Editing Months Before Release
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: The finished cut only came together around four months before the premiere, with Gore Verbinski reportedly putting in 18-hour days in the edit suite to get it done in time. Given the chaos on set, it's a small miracle the film even made its release date.

title: Geoffrey Rush's Left-Side Theory
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: Geoffrey Rush apparently has a theory that most people's eyes are naturally drawn to the left side of a screen first, so as Barbossa he tried to position himself there in shots whenever he could. Whether or not the theory holds up, it's a nice bit of insight into how deliberately he built the performance.

title: Will Turner Nearly Went to Heath Ledger
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: The role of Will Turner came down to a straight choice between Orlando Bloom and Heath Ledger. Bloom's stock had just shot up thanks to Lord of the Rings, and that timing is generally credited with tipping the casting in his favour.

title: The Black Pearl Was a Real, Working Ship
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: Rather than relying purely on effects, the production built a full-size, genuinely seaworthy replica of the Black Pearl for filming. That physical ship went on to become just as much a symbol of the franchise as any of the actors.

title: Hans Zimmer Was Behind the Score
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: The soundtrack is officially credited to Klaus Badelt, but it was produced under Hans Zimmer, whose fingerprints are all over that big, driving adventure sound the franchise became known for.

title: Disney's First PG-13 Film
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
description: Every Walt Disney Pictures release up to this point had been rated G or PG, so putting out a PG-13 pirate movie was a genuine departure for the studio, and one that plenty of people internally, including Eisner himself, were nervous about.

title: It Was Almost Called Vengeance
description: Before it settled on the simple, blunt title we all know, Matt Reeves' film was going by the working title 'Vengeance' during production. Given how much the movie leans into Bruce's obsession with payback (and that improvised line he screams at the train station), it's honestly a fitting alternate name.

title: Kurt Cobain Was the Blueprint
description: Reeves has said he had Nirvana's 'Something In The Way' on repeat while writing the first act, and that's what led him away from the classic playboy Bruce Wayne. Instead he pictured a grieving recluse holed up in a decaying mansion, basically a fictionalised Kurt Cobain in a cape.

title: The First Batman to Actually Wear Eyeliner
description: Every other live-action Batman has taken the cowl off and the black eye makeup just magically vanishes. This is the first version to actually address it, with Bruce's smudged, running eye makeup treated as part of the character rather than a continuity error nobody talks about.

title: Pattinson Lied to Christopher Nolan to Audition
description: Pattinson's screen test for the role happened in May 2019 while he was mid-rehearsal for Tenet in LA. He told Nolan he had a family emergency to slip away, and Nolan immediately clocked what was actually going on and called him out on it.

title: Penguin's Whole Vibe Is Fredo Corleone
description: Reeves has pointed to Fredo from The Godfather as a direct inspiration for Colin Farrell's Oswald Cobblepot, the idea being a guy everyone underestimates and writes off, but who's actually got real ambition and menace bubbling under the surface.

title: Barry Keoghan's Joker Nearly Got Cut Entirely
description: That brief, unsettling Arkham scene where Keoghan's scarred prisoner chats with Riddler almost didn't make the final cut of the movie. It's easy to miss on a first watch, but it's the character's first live-action appearance in this new universe.

title: Zoë Kravitz Voiced Catwoman Years Before Playing Her
description: Kravitz's history with Selina Kyle didn't start on this film's set. She actually voiced Catwoman for a cameo appearance back in 2017's The Lego Batman Movie, years before Reeves cast her in the live-action role.

title: She Also Auditioned for Catwoman a Decade Earlier
description: Kravitz tried out for a small, unnamed role in 2012's The Dark Knight Rises and was reportedly told the studio wasn't going 'urban' for that part. A story she's told a couple of times since, long before Selina Kyle ever ended up being hers.

title: The Toughest Lighting Job of the DP's Career
description: Cinematographer Greig Fraser called this the most complicated lighting job he'd ever tackled, saying the real challenge was finding the right balance of darkness and light specifically for how Batman himself needed to look on screen.

title: Every Batman Costume Comes With the Same Warning
description: There's apparently a tradition of Batman actors passing down survival tips. Pattinson got advice from Christian Bale, and Kravitz got hers from Michelle Pfeiffer, and it all boiled down to the same practical thing: figure out how you're going to use the toilet while wearing that suit.

title: The Batmobile Is Basically a 1970s Comic Come to Life
description: Instead of the usual sleek, gadget-laden tank, this Batmobile is a stripped-down muscle car, and that's a deliberate nod to the Neal Adams comics from the 70s, where the car was meant to look ordinary enough for stealth rather than intimidation.

title: Penguin's Face Was Built From Six Separate Pieces
description: Colin Farrell's prosthetics were made up of six distinct pieces glued together for every shooting day, and the crew would shine harsh flashlights directly at his face before he was allowed on set, just to make sure none of the seams were visible on camera.

title: Reeves Wrote the Script to a Taxi Driver Needle Drop
description: While hammering out the screenplay, Reeves reportedly kept 'Thank God for the Rain' from the Taxi Driver soundtrack on loop, which tracks given how much of that film's lonely, paranoid energy bleeds into this version of Gotham.

title: The Comic Book Homework Behind the Script
description: Reeves has named three specific comics as his main touchstones for the film: Batman: Ego, Batman: The Long Halloween, and Batman: Year One, alongside 70s films Chinatown and Klute for the general mood and detective-noir feel he was chasing.

title: Paul Dano Got Handed a Riddler Comic Series Afterwards
description: His take on the Riddler impressed DC enough that they brought him on to actually write a six-issue comic series, Riddler: Year One, exploring his own version of the character's backstory for their Black Label imprint.

title: The Opening Robbery Is a Sneaky Robert Pattinson Callback
description: Keep an eye on the convenience store that gets robbed early on, it's called 'Good Times Groceries'. That's a wink to Good Time, the 2017 Safdie Brothers film starring Pattinson, which Reeves watched and reportedly started writing this script with Pattinson already in mind for Batman.

title: The Iceberg Lounge Finally Makes Its Movie Debut
description: Penguin's posh nightclub has been a staple of the comics since 1995, but this is genuinely the first time it's ever shown up on the big screen, serving as his base of operations and the movie's seediest hub of Gotham corruption.

title: That Cowl Owes a Debt to Adam West
description: Every big-screen Batman before this had a pointy, beak-like nose on the cowl. Pattinson's version swaps that out for a rounder nose piece, which looks a lot closer to what Adam West wore in the 1966 series, right down to the visible stitching if you look closely enough.

title: Commissioner Savage's Name Is a Deep Cut
description: Alex Ferns' doomed Commissioner Pete Savage shares his surname with a character from a 1966 Batman TV series episode called 'An Egg Grows in Gotham', where Pete Savage is a descendant of one of Gotham's founding families. The characters aren't connected, but it's hard to believe Reeves picked that name by accident given his soft spot for the old show.

title: 'I'm Vengeance' Wasn't in the Script
description: That now-iconic growl at the end of the train station beatdown was completely improvised by Pattinson on the day. He's said he wanted to say it right as the guy was losing consciousness, so it would burrow into his dreams and properly mess him up.

title: Pattinson Auditioned Wearing Two Old Batsuits
description: For his audition, Pattinson didn't get a custom suit, he was put in Val Kilmer's actual Batman Forever costume. The cowl was way too big and made him look like a bobblehead, so the crew swapped it for George Clooney's cowl from Batman & Robin instead. Funnily enough, Christian Bale went through basically the same setup for his own Dark Knight screen test years earlier.

title: Riddler's Apartment Was Watching the Iceberg Lounge the Whole Time
description: Eagle-eyed viewers on HBO Max spotted that Riddler's rundown apartment sits directly across from the Iceberg Lounge, the exact spot where most of his incriminating evidence photos would've been taken. Reeves personally confirmed the detail was intentional once fans clocked it.

title: A Throwaway Line Name-Drops Dick Grayson's Future City
description: There's a mention of Blüdhaven tucked into the film, the neighbouring city that first showed up in 1996's Nightwing #1 comic. In the wider DC mythology it's where Dick Grayson eventually sets up shop as Nightwing, so it's a nice bit of world-building for anyone who clocked it.

title: The Film's Whole Arc Comes From One Comic's Big Idea
description: By the end of the movie Bruce consciously shifts his mission away from vengeance and toward hope for Gotham. That exact turn is lifted straight from the graphic novel Batman: Ego, which Reeves has repeatedly cited as one of the single biggest influences on the whole film.
